---- MODULE W4Od18m3p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

\* Smart-home hubs elect a coordinator; only the current coordinator's writes
\* to the shared lock-policy record are accepted, and only when the writer
\* quoted the version it actually read.
CONSTANTS Hubs, MaxTerm, MaxVersion, MaxInflight

VARIABLES leader, term, record, inflight, history
vars == <<leader, term, record, inflight, history>>

Notes == [src: Hubs, term: 1..MaxTerm, base: 0..MaxVersion]
Entries == [writer: Hubs, base: 0..MaxVersion]
First == CHOOSE h \in Hubs : TRUE

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Hubs
  /\ term \in 1..MaxTerm
  /\ record \in [version: 0..MaxVersion, writer: Hubs]
  /\ inflight \subseteq Notes
  /\ history \in Seq(Entries)

\* An edit is installable only while it is term-current, authored by the
\* incumbent coordinator, and quoting the version now on the record.
Installable(m) ==
  /\ m.term = term
  /\ m.src = leader
  /\ m.base = record.version
  /\ record.version < MaxVersion

Init ==
  /\ leader = First
  /\ term = 1
  /\ record = [version |-> 0, writer |-> First]
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ history = <<>>

\* Failover promotes a different hub and bumps the coordination term.
Failover ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ \E h \in Hubs :
       /\ h # leader
       /\ leader' = h
       /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, inflight, history>>

\* A hub emits an edit quoting whatever term and version it last observed;
\* the network buffer is a set, so delivery order is unconstrained.
Propose ==
  /\ Cardinality(inflight) < MaxInflight
  /\ \E h \in Hubs, t \in 1..term, b \in 0..record.version :
       inflight' = inflight \cup {[src |-> h, term |-> t, base |-> b]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, record, history>>

Apply ==
  /\ \E m \in inflight :
       /\ m.term = term
       /\ m.src = leader
       /\ m.base = record.version
       /\ record.version < MaxVersion
       /\ record' = [version |-> record.version + 1, writer |-> m.src]
       /\ history' = Append(history, [writer |-> m.src, base |-> m.base])
       /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Reject ==
  /\ \E m \in inflight :
       /\ ~Installable(m)
       /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, record, history>>

Next == Failover \/ Propose \/ Apply \/ Reject

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No edit is ever silently overwritten: the n-th accepted edit was computed
\* against exactly the record left behind by the (n-1)-th accepted edit.
NoLostUpdate == \A i \in 1..Len(history) : history[i].base = i - 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Hubs = {h1, h2}
  MaxTerm = 2
  MaxVersion = 2
  MaxInflight = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps one shared lock-policy record that every hub in the house can edit. Because any hub may go dark, the hubs run a coordinator election: exactly one hub holds the coordinator role at a time, and each election round is stamped with a monotonically increasing term number.

The shared record carries a version counter and the identity of the hub that last wrote it. A hub that wants to change the policy reads the record and emits an edit that quotes the term it believes is current and the version number it read. Edits travel over the home mesh network, which gives no ordering guarantee at all: the pending edits sit in an unordered buffer and may be delivered in any order, so an edit issued against an old version can easily arrive after a newer edit has already landed.

The system has four actions. Failover promotes some hub other than the incumbent to coordinator and increments the term, up to a fixed maximum number of terms. Propose lets any hub place a new edit into the pending buffer, quoting any term no later than the current one and any version no later than the current record version, provided the buffer still has room. An edit counts as installable when its term matches the current term, its author is the current coordinator, its quoted version equals the record's present version, and the record has not yet reached its final version. Apply takes any installable pending edit and installs it, bumps the version by one, records the author, and appends the edit to the accepted history. Reject removes any pending edit that is not installable, discarding it without touching the record.

The accepted history is the audit trail of the policy record. Each entry stores the author and the version that author was editing against.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The n-th entry of the accepted history always quotes base version n-1, so every accepted edit was computed against exactly the record state left by the previously accepted edit and no hub's write is ever silently overwritten.

---- MODULE W4Od13m1p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Vending machines sit on a circulating-token ring.  A single promotional
\* item exists network-wide; dispensing it is irreversible, so the ledger
\* records exactly which machine consumed it.
CONSTANTS N, MaxOverrides

Machines == 1..N
None == 0
Nxt(m) == (m % N) + 1

VARIABLES holder, waiting, asked, dispensed, redeemer, overrides
vars == <<holder, waiting, asked, dispensed, redeemer, overrides>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in Machines
  /\ waiting \subseteq Machines
  /\ asked \subseteq Machines
  /\ dispensed \subseteq Machines
  /\ redeemer \in Machines \cup {None}
  /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
  /\ holder = 1
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ asked = {}
  /\ dispensed = {}
  /\ redeemer = None
  /\ overrides = MaxOverrides

\* A customer walks up to a machine that has not yet taken a promo request.
Request ==
  /\ \E m \in Machines :
       /\ m \notin asked
       /\ asked' = asked \cup {m}
       /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, dispensed, redeemer, overrides>>

Circulate ==
  /\ holder' = Nxt(holder)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, asked, dispensed, redeemer, overrides>>

\* The promo is still unclaimed, so the token holder physically dispenses it
\* and writes itself into the network ledger.
Redeem ==
  /\ holder \in waiting
  /\ redeemer = None
  /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {holder}
  /\ redeemer' = holder
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {holder}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, asked, overrides>>

Decline ==
  /\ holder \in waiting
  /\ redeemer # None
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {holder}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, asked, dispensed, redeemer, overrides>>

Serve == Redeem \/ Decline

\* A field technician's master key may relocate the token, bypassing ring
\* order, but the key has a limited number of uses.
AdminRelocate ==
  /\ overrides > 0
  /\ \E m \in Machines :
       /\ m # holder
       /\ holder' = m
  /\ overrides' = overrides - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, asked, dispensed, redeemer>>

Next == Request \/ Circulate \/ Redeem \/ Decline \/ AdminRelocate

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Circulate) /\ SF_vars(Serve)

\* Every machine that actually put the promo item in a customer's hands is
\* the single machine the ledger names, so the item leaves stock once.
OneTimeDispense == \A m \in dispensed : m = redeemer

EveryRequestResolved == \A m \in Machines : (m \in waiting) ~> (m \notin waiting)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  N = 3
  MaxOverrides = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OneTimeDispense

PROPERTY EveryRequestResolved
nl:
A regional vending machine network runs a promotion in which exactly one promotional item exists across the whole fleet. Dispensing that item is irreversible: once a machine drops it into a customer's hands there is nothing to take back, so the network keeps a ledger naming the single machine that consumed it. The machines are wired in a ring and a circulating token travels around it; a machine only interacts with the shared promotion while it is holding the token.

There are five actions. Request models a customer walking up to a machine that has not yet taken a promo request in this campaign, adding that machine to the set of machines with a waiting customer and marking it as having asked. Circulate advances the token from its current machine to the next machine around the ring. Redeem fires when the token holder has a waiting customer and the ledger still shows the promotion unclaimed: the machine physically dispenses the item, writes itself into the ledger as the redeemer, and clears its waiting customer. Decline fires when the token holder has a waiting customer but the ledger already names a redeemer: the customer is told the promotion is over and the machine clears its waiting customer without dispensing anything. AdminRelocate is a privileged field-technician override that teleports the token to any other machine, bypassing ring order entirely; the master key has a fixed limited number of uses, after which the ring circulates on its own again.

Because the promotional item cannot be un-dispensed, the interesting question is not who holds the token but how many times stock actually leaves the fleet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every machine recorded as having physically dispensed the promotional item is the one machine the network ledger names as the redeemer, so the irreversible dispense happens at most once across the entire fleet.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every machine that acquires a waiting promo customer eventually has that customer resolved, either by dispensing the item or by being told the promotion is already claimed.

---- MODULE W4Od8m0p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Two registration portals share one seat pool for a course.  Each portal
\* drafts an enrolment against a catalog snapshot and commits only if the
\* catalog version it read is still current -- otherwise it re-reads.
CONSTANTS Seats, Portals, MaxVersion, MaxRetry

VARIABLES pool, held, catalogVer, draft, drafting, retries
vars == <<pool, held, catalogVer, draft, drafting, retries>>

Owned == UNION {held[p] : p \in Portals}
AnySeat == CHOOSE s \in Seats : TRUE

TypeOK ==
  /\ pool \subseteq Seats
  /\ held \in [Portals -> SUBSET Seats]
  /\ catalogVer \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ draft \in [Portals -> [seat: Seats, snap: 0..MaxVersion]]
  /\ drafting \subseteq Portals
  /\ retries \in [Portals -> 0..MaxRetry]

Init ==
  /\ pool = Seats
  /\ held = [p \in Portals |-> {}]
  /\ catalogVer = 0
  /\ draft = [p \in Portals |-> [seat |-> AnySeat, snap |-> 0]]
  /\ drafting = {}
  /\ retries = [p \in Portals |-> 0]

Committable(p) ==
  /\ p \in drafting
  /\ draft[p].snap = catalogVer
  /\ draft[p].seat \in pool
  /\ catalogVer < MaxVersion

\* A portal reads the catalog and names a seat it believes is free.
Snapshot(p) ==
  /\ p \notin drafting
  /\ \E s \in Seats :
       draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![p] = [seat |-> s, snap |-> catalogVer]]
  /\ drafting' = drafting \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, catalogVer, retries>>

\* The seat leaves the shared pool and enters exactly one portal's roster.
Enrol(p) ==
  /\ Committable(p)
  /\ pool' = pool \ {draft[p].seat}
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {draft[p].seat}]
  /\ catalogVer' = catalogVer + 1
  /\ drafting' = drafting \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, retries>>

Restart(p) ==
  /\ p \in drafting
  /\ ~Committable(p)
  /\ drafting' = drafting \ {p}
  /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![p] = IF @ < MaxRetry THEN @ + 1 ELSE @]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, held, catalogVer, draft>>

Withdraw(p) ==
  /\ catalogVer < MaxVersion
  /\ \E s \in held[p] :
       /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![p] = @ \ {s}]
       /\ pool' = pool \cup {s}
  /\ catalogVer' = catalogVer + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, drafting, retries>>

Next == \E p \in Portals : Snapshot(p) \/ Enrol(p) \/ Restart(p) \/ Withdraw(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Seats are neither minted nor lost: the free pool and the union of the two
\* portals' rosters tile the seat set exactly, with no overlap.
SeatConservation ==
  /\ pool \cup Owned = Seats
  /\ Cardinality(pool) + Cardinality(Owned) = Cardinality(Seats)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Seats = {s1, s2, s3}
  Portals = {web, desk}
  MaxVersion = 2
  MaxRetry = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatConservation
nl:
A university runs two independent course-registration portals -- for example a web front end and a phone-in desk -- that both draw from a single shared pool of seats in one course. There is no lock on the pool. Instead the shared catalog carries a version number, and each portal works optimistically: it takes a snapshot and then tries to commit, discovering only at commit time whether the world moved underneath it.

The state consists of the free seat pool, a per-portal roster of seats that portal has placed students into, the catalog version counter, a per-portal draft record (a seat name and the catalog version snapshotted with it), the set of portals that currently have a draft open, and a per-portal retry counter that saturates at a fixed maximum.

There are four actions, each performed by one of the two portals. Snapshot fires when the portal has no draft open: the portal reads the current catalog version and names any seat it intends to fill, writes both into its draft record, and joins the set of portals with an open draft. A draft is committable when it is open, its recorded version still equals the live catalog version, the seat it names is still in the free pool, and the catalog has not reached its final version. Enrol fires on a committable draft: the named seat leaves the free pool, joins that portal's roster, the catalog version advances by one, and the portal's draft is closed. Restart fires on an open draft that is not committable: the portal closes the draft without effect, bumps its saturating retry counter, and will read the catalog again from scratch. Withdraw lets a portal return one seat from its own roster to the free pool, again advancing the catalog version.

Seats are physical capacity in a lecture hall. The registration system may hand a seat to a portal or take it back, but it must never conjure a seat that the hall does not have, and it must never lose one into a gap between the two portals.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The free pool together with the union of both portals' rosters always covers the entire seat set, and their sizes add up to exactly the number of seats, so every seat sits in exactly one place at every moment and none is created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od7m0p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* Cranes shuffle boxes between three yard areas.  A crane plans a move
\* against a manifest revision and commits only if that revision still
\* holds; otherwise it re-reads, a bounded number of times.
CONSTANTS Cranes, Fleet, MaxRev, MaxReread, MaxForce

Areas == {"apron", "gantry", "hold"}
Lanes == {mv \in Areas \X Areas : mv[1] # mv[2]}
Park == CHOOSE mv \in Lanes : TRUE
Orders == [st: {"idle", "open", "shut"}, lane: Lanes, snap: 0..MaxRev]

VARIABLES stack, rev, order, reread, forceLeft
vars == <<stack, rev, order, reread, forceLeft>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ stack \in [Areas -> 0..Fleet]
  /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
  /\ order \in [Cranes -> Orders]
  /\ reread \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxReread]
  /\ forceLeft \in 0..MaxForce

Blank(s) == [st |-> s, lane |-> Park, snap |-> 0]

Init ==
  /\ stack = [a \in Areas |-> IF a = "apron" THEN Fleet ELSE 0]
  /\ rev = 0
  /\ order = [c \in Cranes |-> Blank("idle")]
  /\ reread = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
  /\ forceLeft = MaxForce

Open(c) == order[c].st = "open"
Loaded(c) == stack[order[c].lane[1]] > 0
Shift(c) == stack' = [stack EXCEPT ![order[c].lane[1]] = @ - 1,
                                   ![order[c].lane[2]] = @ + 1]

Plan(c) ==
  /\ order[c].st = "idle"
  /\ \E mv \in Lanes :
       order' = [order EXCEPT ![c] = [st |-> "open", lane |-> mv, snap |-> rev]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, rev, reread, forceLeft>>

\* Optimistic commit: the revision the crane read must still be live.
Commit(c) ==
  /\ Open(c) /\ order[c].snap = rev /\ Loaded(c) /\ rev < MaxRev
  /\ Shift(c)
  /\ rev' = rev + 1
  /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![c] = Blank("shut")]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reread, forceLeft>>

Reread(c) ==
  /\ Open(c) /\ order[c].snap # rev /\ reread[c] < MaxReread
  /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![c].snap = rev]
  /\ reread' = [reread EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, rev, forceLeft>>

\* Yard supervisor's key: pushes a plan through with no revision check,
\* still shifting exactly one box out of one area and into another.
Force(c) ==
  /\ Open(c) /\ forceLeft > 0 /\ Loaded(c) /\ rev < MaxRev
  /\ Shift(c)
  /\ rev' = rev + 1
  /\ forceLeft' = forceLeft - 1
  /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![c] = Blank("shut")]
  /\ UNCHANGED reread

Abandon(c) ==
  /\ Open(c)
  /\ \/ order[c].snap = rev /\ (~Loaded(c) \/ rev = MaxRev)
     \/ order[c].snap # rev /\ reread[c] = MaxReread
  /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![c] = Blank("shut")]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stack, rev, reread, forceLeft>>

\* With no open work left the yard simply stands still.
Settle == (\A c \in Cranes : order[c].st = "shut") /\ UNCHANGED vars

Retire == \E c \in Cranes : Commit(c) \/ Force(c) \/ Abandon(c)
Refresh == \E c \in Cranes : Reread(c)

Next == (\E c \in Cranes : Plan(c)) \/ Retire \/ Refresh \/ Settle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Retire) /\ WF_vars(Refresh)

\* Boxes are only ever shifted between areas, never created or destroyed.
BoxConservation == stack["apron"] + stack["gantry"] + stack["hold"] = Fleet

EveryPlanRetired == \A c \in Cranes : Open(c) ~> (order[c].st = "shut")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cranes = {cr1, cr2}
  Fleet = 2
  MaxRev = 2
  MaxReread = 1
  MaxForce = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BoxConservation

PROPERTY EveryPlanRetired
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is divided into three areas: the apron, the gantry lane, and the ship's hold. A fixed fleet of boxes starts stacked on the apron. Several cranes work the yard concurrently. There is no reservation desk; instead the yard keeps a shared manifest with a revision number, and each crane works optimistically: it plans a move against the revision it read, and its commit succeeds only if that revision is still the live one.

Each crane carries an order record with a status of idle, open, or shut, plus the lane it wants to work (a source area and a distinct destination area) and the manifest revision it snapshotted. When an order is idle or shut its lane and revision fields are reset to a fixed parked default. Each crane also has a bounded re-read allowance, and the yard holds a bounded number of supervisor override uses.

There are six actions. Plan fires for an idle crane: it chooses any lane with distinct endpoints, stamps the current manifest revision onto its order, and marks the order open. Commit fires when the crane's stamped revision still equals the live revision, the source area actually has a box, and the manifest has not reached its final revision: exactly one box leaves the source area, exactly one box arrives in the destination area, the revision advances, and the order is reset to shut. Reread fires when an open order's stamped revision is stale and the crane still has re-read allowance left: the crane restamps the order with the live revision and spends one allowance. Force is a privileged yard-supervisor override: given remaining override uses, it pushes an open order through with no revision check at all, still moving exactly one box from source to destination, advancing the revision, consuming one override, and shutting the order. Settle fires only when every crane's order is already shut and simply leaves the yard exactly as it stands. Abandon shuts an open order that can no longer make progress -- either its revision is current but the source area is empty or the manifest is at its final revision, or its revision is stale and its re-read allowance is spent.

Boxes are physical cargo. Cranes relocate them between the three areas; nothing in the yard manufactures or scraps a box.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of boxes on the apron plus the number in the gantry lane plus the number in the hold always equals the original fleet size, so every move conserves cargo exactly and no box is ever created or destroyed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every crane whose order is open eventually reaches a shut order, whether by committing the move, having the supervisor force it through, or abandoning it.

---- MODULE W4Od18m4p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* Hubs queue deadbolt commands; the queue is bounded, so a hub whose
\* command finds it full is pushed back instead of buffered.  Only the hub
\* the driver names may actually turn the bolt motor.
CONSTANTS Hubs, Depth, MaxPushback

NoDriver == "none"

VARIABLES pipe, phase, driver, bolt, pushback
vars == <<pipe, phase, driver, bolt, pushback>>

Phases == {"idle", "queued", "turning", "gone"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ pipe \in Seq(Hubs)
  /\ Len(pipe) =< Depth
  /\ phase \in [Hubs -> Phases]
  /\ driver \in Hubs \cup {NoDriver}
  /\ bolt \in {"locked", "open"}
  /\ pushback \in 0..MaxPushback

Init ==
  /\ pipe = <<>>
  /\ phase = [h \in Hubs |-> "idle"]
  /\ driver = NoDriver
  /\ bolt = "locked"
  /\ pushback = 0

Enqueue(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "idle"
  /\ Len(pipe) < Depth
  /\ pipe' = Append(pipe, h)
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "queued"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<driver, bolt, pushback>>

\* Backpressure: a full pipe refuses the command outright.
Refuse(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "idle"
  /\ Len(pipe) = Depth
  /\ pushback < MaxPushback
  /\ pushback' = pushback + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pipe, phase, driver, bolt>>

\* The bolt motor is handed to exactly one hub at a time.
Dispatch ==
  /\ driver = NoDriver
  /\ pipe # <<>>
  /\ LET h == Head(pipe) IN
       /\ phase[h] = "queued"
       /\ driver' = h
       /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "turning"]
  /\ pipe' = Tail(pipe)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bolt, pushback>>

\* A command whose author is no longer queued is dropped from the pipe.
Drain ==
  /\ driver = NoDriver
  /\ pipe # <<>>
  /\ phase[Head(pipe)] # "queued"
  /\ pipe' = Tail(pipe)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, driver, bolt, pushback>>

Turn(h) ==
  /\ driver = h
  /\ phase[h] = "turning"
  /\ bolt' = IF bolt = "locked" THEN "open" ELSE "locked"
  /\ driver' = NoDriver
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pipe, pushback>>

\* A hub can drop off the mesh without telling anyone.
Vanish(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] \in {"queued", "turning"}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "gone"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pipe, driver, bolt, pushback>>

Reclaim ==
  /\ driver # NoDriver
  /\ phase[driver] = "gone"
  /\ driver' = NoDriver
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pipe, phase, bolt, pushback>>

Rejoin(h) ==
  /\ phase[h] = "gone"
  /\ driver # h
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pipe, driver, bolt, pushback>>

Next == \E h \in Hubs :
  Enqueue(h) \/ Refuse(h) \/ Dispatch \/ Drain \/ Turn(h) \/ Vanish(h) \/ Reclaim \/ Rejoin(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Any hub whose motor phase says it is turning the bolt must be the hub the
\* motor driver names, so two hubs never drive the deadbolt at once.
BoltExclusion == \A h \in Hubs : (phase[h] = "turning") => (driver = h)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Hubs = {front, back}
  Depth = 2
  MaxPushback = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BoltExclusion
nl:
A smart-home door lock network has several hubs that all want to drive the same physical deadbolt motor on the front door. Commands are not applied directly. Instead each hub pushes a command into a shared command pipe of bounded depth, and a dispatcher hands the motor to one hub at a time. Because the pipe is bounded, a hub arriving at a full pipe is pushed back rather than buffered, and the network counts how many pushbacks it has issued up to a fixed ceiling.

The state is the command pipe (a sequence of hub names), a phase for each hub which is idle, queued, turning, or gone, the name of the hub the motor driver currently names (or none), the bolt position, and the pushback counter.

There are eight actions. Enqueue fires for an idle hub when the pipe still has room: the hub is appended to the pipe and moves to queued. Refuse is the backpressure path: an idle hub arriving at a full pipe is turned away, the pushback counter advances, and nothing else changes. Dispatch fires when the motor driver names nobody and the pipe is non-empty: the hub at the head of the pipe, provided it is still queued, becomes the named driver and moves to turning, and the pipe advances. Drain fires when the motor driver names nobody and the hub at the head of the pipe is no longer queued: that stale command is simply dropped from the pipe. Turn fires for the hub the driver names while that hub is turning: the bolt flips between locked and open, the driver is released back to none, and the hub returns to idle. Vanish models a hub dropping off the mesh without telling anyone: a queued or turning hub silently becomes gone. Reclaim lets the dispatcher release the motor when the hub it names has gone. Rejoin brings a gone hub that the motor no longer names back to idle.

The bolt motor is a single piece of hardware. Two hubs energising it at once would strip the mechanism, so the whole pipe-and-dispatcher arrangement exists to keep exactly one hub attached to the motor.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every hub whose phase says it is turning the bolt is the very hub that the motor driver names, so at no reachable state do two different hubs both hold the deadbolt motor.

---- MODULE W4Od13m4p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* Machines file sales reports into a bounded intake belt; the back office
\* folds them one at a time into the fleet's shared inventory record.  The
\* office may die silently while holding a report.
CONSTANTS Reports, Belt

NoWork == 0

VARIABLES belt, taken, folded, holding, officeUp
vars == <<belt, taken, folded, holding, officeUp>>

OnBelt(r) == \E i \in 1..Len(belt) : belt[i] = r

TypeOK ==
  /\ belt \in Seq(Reports)
  /\ Len(belt) =< Belt
  /\ taken \subseteq Reports
  /\ folded \subseteq Reports
  /\ holding \in Reports \cup {NoWork}
  /\ officeUp \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ belt = <<>>
  /\ taken = {}
  /\ folded = {}
  /\ holding = NoWork
  /\ officeUp = TRUE

\* Backpressure: a machine can only file while the belt has slack.
File ==
  /\ Len(belt) < Belt
  /\ \E r \in Reports \ taken :
       /\ belt' = Append(belt, r)
       /\ taken' = taken \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<folded, holding, officeUp>>

Pick ==
  /\ officeUp
  /\ holding = NoWork
  /\ belt # <<>>
  /\ holding' = Head(belt)
  /\ belt' = Tail(belt)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<taken, folded, officeUp>>

\* Folding is the only step that changes the shared inventory record.
Fold ==
  /\ officeUp
  /\ holding # NoWork
  /\ folded' = folded \cup {holding}
  /\ holding' = NoWork
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, taken, officeUp>>

Die ==
  /\ officeUp
  /\ officeUp' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, taken, folded, holding>>

\* Restarting keeps whatever report was in hand, so nothing in flight is
\* silently discarded by the crash.
Restart ==
  /\ ~officeUp
  /\ officeUp' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, taken, folded, holding>>

Serve == Pick \/ Fold
Next == File \/ Pick \/ Fold \/ Die \/ Restart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Serve) /\ WF_vars(Restart)

\* Every report the fleet accepted is accounted for somewhere: already folded
\* into the shared record, still on the belt, or in the office's hand.
NoReportLost ==
  \A r \in taken : r \in folded \/ OnBelt(r) \/ r = holding

EveryReportFolded == \A r \in Reports : (r \in taken) ~> (r \in folded)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Reports = {r1, r2, r3}
  Belt = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoReportLost

PROPERTY EveryReportFolded
nl:
A vending machine network keeps one shared inventory record for the whole fleet. Machines do not write to that record directly. Each machine files a sales report onto a shared intake belt of bounded length, and a single back-office process picks reports off the belt one at a time and folds each into the shared record. Because the belt is bounded, a machine can only file a report while the belt still has slack -- that is the backpressure.

The state is the intake belt (a sequence of report identifiers), the set of reports the fleet has accepted for filing, the set of reports already folded into the shared record, the report currently in the back office's hand (or none), and a flag saying whether the back office is running.

There are five actions. File fires when the belt has slack: some report that has not been accepted yet is appended to the belt and added to the accepted set. Pick fires when the back office is running with empty hands and the belt is non-empty: it takes the report at the head of the belt into its hand and the belt advances. Fold fires when the running back office has a report in hand: that report is folded into the shared inventory record and the hand is emptied. Die models the back office crashing silently -- nothing announces it, and whatever report was in hand stays in hand. Restart brings the back office back up with the in-hand report still there, so a crash never quietly throws away work that was already taken off the belt.

The point of the arrangement is that the shared inventory record must end up reflecting every report the fleet accepted. A report is in exactly one of three places at all times: folded into the record, waiting on the belt, or held by the office.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every report the fleet has accepted for filing is either already folded into the shared inventory record, still sitting on the intake belt, or in the back office's hand, so no accepted update is ever dropped on the floor.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every report the fleet accepts is eventually folded into the shared inventory record.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m4p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* Issuing a blood unit is irreversible: it leaves the fridge for a patient
\* and cannot come back.  Requests wait in a bounded worklist; a technician
\* may collapse silently while holding one, and the recovery path must never
\* put an already-issued unit back on the worklist.
CONSTANTS Units, Worklist, MaxTurnaway

Nothing == "nothing"

VARIABLES fridge, work, issued, inHand, turnaway
vars == <<fridge, work, issued, inHand, turnaway>>

Listed(u) == \E i \in 1..Len(work) : work[i] = u

TypeOK ==
  /\ fridge \subseteq Units
  /\ work \in Seq(Units)
  /\ Len(work) =< Worklist
  /\ issued \subseteq Units
  /\ inHand \in Units \cup {Nothing}
  /\ turnaway \in 0..MaxTurnaway

Init ==
  /\ fridge = Units
  /\ work = <<>>
  /\ issued = {}
  /\ inHand = Nothing
  /\ turnaway = 0

Listable(u) == u \in fridge /\ ~Listed(u) /\ u # inHand
CanOrder == Len(work) < Worklist /\ \E u \in Units : Listable(u)

Order ==
  /\ CanOrder
  /\ \E u \in Units :
       /\ Listable(u)
       /\ work' = Append(work, u)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, issued, inHand, turnaway>>

\* Backpressure: when nothing can be listed the ward is turned away and the
\* refusal is tallied, saturating at the ceiling.
TurnAway ==
  /\ ~CanOrder
  /\ turnaway' = IF turnaway < MaxTurnaway THEN turnaway + 1 ELSE turnaway
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, work, issued, inHand>>

Take ==
  /\ inHand = Nothing
  /\ work # <<>>
  /\ inHand' = Head(work)
  /\ work' = Tail(work)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, issued, turnaway>>

\* The irreversible step: the unit leaves stock and is logged as issued.
Issue ==
  /\ inHand # Nothing
  /\ inHand \in fridge
  /\ fridge' = fridge \ {inHand}
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {inHand}
  /\ inHand' = Nothing
  /\ UNCHANGED <<work, turnaway>>

\* Technician collapses; the unit in hand is only relisted if stock still
\* shows it, which is what keeps a crash from causing a second issue.
Collapse ==
  /\ inHand # Nothing
  /\ IF inHand \in fridge /\ Len(work) < Worklist
       THEN work' = Append(work, inHand)
       ELSE work' = work
  /\ inHand' = Nothing
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, issued, turnaway>>

Next == Order \/ TurnAway \/ Take \/ Issue \/ Collapse

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Once a unit has gone out to a patient it is gone from stock, absent from
\* the worklist, and out of any technician's hand -- so it can never be
\* issued a second time.
IssuedOnlyOnce ==
  \A u \in issued : u \notin fridge /\ ~Listed(u) /\ u # inHand
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Units = {u1, u2, u3}
  Worklist = 2
  MaxTurnaway = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT IssuedOnlyOnce
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker manages a fridge of labelled units. Issuing a unit to a patient is irreversible: once it leaves the fridge it is transfused or spoiled and can never be returned to stock. Ward requests do not reach the fridge directly; they sit on a worklist of bounded length, and a single technician works the list. When nothing can be listed -- either the worklist is full or no unit is eligible -- the tracker applies backpressure and turns the ward away instead of buffering, tallying turnaways up to a fixed ceiling at which the tally saturates.

The state is the set of units still in the fridge, the worklist (a sequence of unit labels), the set of units already issued, the unit in the technician's hand (or nothing), and the turnaway counter.

There are five actions. A unit is listable when it is still in the fridge, is not already on the worklist, and is not in the technician's hand. Order appends some listable unit to the worklist, provided the worklist has room. TurnAway is the backpressure path and fires exactly when no listable unit can be added: the request is refused and the turnaway tally advances, saturating at its ceiling. Take moves the head of the worklist into the technician's empty hand. Issue is the irreversible step: the unit in hand, provided stock still shows it, leaves the fridge, is written into the issued log, and the hand is emptied. Collapse models the technician going down silently mid-task: the unit in hand is relisted at the back of the worklist only if stock still shows it and the list has room, and otherwise is simply released; either way the hand is emptied.

The whole design turns on that guard inside Collapse. A recovery path that blindly relisted whatever was in hand would let an already-transfused unit be picked up and issued a second time, which in a blood bank is a fatal accounting error rather than a mere retry.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every unit recorded in the issued log is absent from the fridge, absent from the worklist, and not in any technician's hand, so no unit can ever be issued a second time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m7p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* Two drone squadrons draw sector assignments from one shared pool.  Each
\* sector has a compare-and-swap register holding an owner and a generation
\* counter; a drone wins a sector only if the generation it read is intact.
CONSTANTS Alpha, Bravo, Sectors, MaxTry, MaxSorties, MaxGen

Drones == Alpha \cup Bravo
Wings == {"alpha", "bravo"}
WingOf(d) == IF d \in Alpha THEN "alpha" ELSE "bravo"
Vacant == "vacant"
Home == CHOOSE s \in Sectors : TRUE
Blank == [sector |-> Home, gen |-> 0]

VARIABLES reg, mode, post, tries, sorties
vars == <<reg, mode, post, tries, sorties>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in [Sectors -> [owner: Drones \cup {Vacant}, gen: 0..MaxGen]]
  /\ mode \in [Drones -> {"idle", "seeking", "flying", "parked"}]
  /\ post \in [Drones -> [sector: Sectors, gen: 0..MaxGen]]
  /\ tries \in [Drones -> 0..MaxTry]
  /\ sorties \in [Wings -> 0..MaxSorties]

Init ==
  /\ reg = [s \in Sectors |-> [owner |-> Vacant, gen |-> 0]]
  /\ mode = [d \in Drones |-> "idle"]
  /\ post = [d \in Drones |-> Blank]
  /\ tries = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ sorties = [w \in Wings |-> 0]

\* The swap fires only against the exact generation the drone snapshotted.
CasReady(d) ==
  /\ mode[d] = "seeking"
  /\ reg[post[d].sector].owner = Vacant
  /\ reg[post[d].sector].gen = post[d].gen
  /\ reg[post[d].sector].gen < MaxGen
  /\ sorties[WingOf(d)] < MaxSorties

Scan(d) ==
  /\ mode[d] = "idle"
  /\ \E s \in Sectors :
       post' = [post EXCEPT ![d] = [sector |-> s, gen |-> reg[s].gen]]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "seeking"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tries, sorties>>

Swap(d) ==
  /\ CasReady(d)
  /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![post[d].sector] = [owner |-> d, gen |-> @.gen + 1]]
  /\ post' = [post EXCEPT ![d].gen = @ + 1]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "flying"]
  /\ sorties' = [sorties EXCEPT ![WingOf(d)] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED tries

Backoff(d) ==
  /\ mode[d] = "seeking" /\ ~CasReady(d) /\ tries[d] < MaxTry
  /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ post' = [post EXCEPT ![d] = Blank]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, sorties>>

Park(d) ==
  /\ mode[d] = "seeking" /\ ~CasReady(d) /\ tries[d] = MaxTry
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "parked"]
  /\ post' = [post EXCEPT ![d] = Blank]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tries, sorties>>

Land(d) ==
  /\ mode[d] = "flying"
  /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![post[d].sector].owner = Vacant]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ post' = [post EXCEPT ![d] = Blank]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, sorties>>

Settle == (\A d \in Drones : mode[d] = "parked") /\ UNCHANGED vars

Resolve == \E d \in Drones : Swap(d) \/ Backoff(d) \/ Park(d)
Next == (\E d \in Drones : Scan(d) \/ Land(d)) \/ Resolve \/ Settle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Resolve)

\* A drone is airborne over a sector only while that sector's register still
\* names it and still carries the generation it won -- so one sector can
\* never be flown by two drones at once.
NoDoubleAssign ==
  \A d \in Drones :
    (mode[d] = "flying") =>
      /\ reg[post[d].sector].owner = d
      /\ reg[post[d].sector].gen = post[d].gen

SeekingResolved == \A d \in Drones : (mode[d] = "seeking") ~> (mode[d] # "seeking")
====
nl:
A wildfire surveillance operation flies two independent drone squadrons, Alpha and Bravo, over the same fire perimeter. Both squadrons draw sector assignments from one shared pool of sectors -- neither squadron has its own private sectors. Each sector carries a compare-and-swap register holding an owner (a drone, or vacant) and a generation counter that ticks up every time the sector is won.

Each drone is idle, seeking, flying, or parked. A drone also carries a posting: the sector it is interested in and the generation number it read off that sector's register. Each drone has a bounded retry allowance, and each squadron has a bounded sortie budget.

There are six actions. Scan fires for an idle drone: it picks any sector in the shared pool, copies that sector's current generation into its posting, and becomes seeking. A seeking drone is CAS-ready when the sector's register still reads vacant, the register's generation still equals the generation the drone snapshotted, the generation has not reached its ceiling, and the drone's squadron still has sortie budget. Swap fires on a CAS-ready drone: the register is atomically rewritten to name that drone with the generation bumped by one, the drone's posting takes the new generation, the drone becomes flying, and the squadron spends one sortie. Backoff fires on a seeking drone that is not CAS-ready and still has retry allowance: it spends one retry, blanks its posting, and drops back to idle. Park fires on a seeking drone that is not CAS-ready with its retry allowance spent: it blanks its posting and parks permanently. Land fires for a flying drone: the sector's register is released back to vacant while keeping its generation, the drone blanks its posting, and returns to idle. Settle applies only when every drone is parked and leaves the swarm exactly as it stands.

A sector is a piece of airspace. Two drones assigned the same sector at the same time would be a mid-air conflict, which is exactly what the generation check in the compare-and-swap is there to prevent when both squadrons race for the same sector.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any drone that is flying is flying a sector whose register still names that drone and still carries the exact generation the drone won, so a single sector is never allocated to two drones at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every drone that starts seeking a sector eventually stops seeking, either by winning the swap, by backing off, or by parking.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m7p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Controllers admit aircraft to the approach corridor by compare-and-swap
\* on one register holding the admitted count plus a stamp.  A controller
\* may go dark silently between reading the register and swapping it.
CONSTANTS Flights, Controllers, Corridor, MaxStamp

NoFlight == "none"
Fresh == [seen |-> 0, stamp |-> 0, plane |-> NoFlight]

VARIABLES reg, corridor, desk, scratch
vars == <<reg, corridor, desk, scratch>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in [seats: 0..Corridor, stamp: 0..MaxStamp]
  /\ corridor \subseteq Flights
  /\ desk \in [Controllers -> {"clear", "reading", "dark"}]
  /\ scratch \in [Controllers -> [seen: 0..Corridor, stamp: 0..MaxStamp,
                                  plane: Flights \cup {NoFlight}]]

Init ==
  /\ reg = [seats |-> 0, stamp |-> 0]
  /\ corridor = {}
  /\ desk = [c \in Controllers |-> "clear"]
  /\ scratch = [c \in Controllers |-> Fresh]

\* The swap is valid only against the stamp the controller actually read.
Swappable(c) ==
  /\ desk[c] = "reading"
  /\ scratch[c].stamp = reg.stamp
  /\ scratch[c].seen < Corridor
  /\ scratch[c].plane \notin corridor
  /\ reg.stamp < MaxStamp

Read(c) ==
  /\ desk[c] = "clear"
  /\ \E f \in Flights :
       scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![c] = [seen |-> reg.seats,
                                          stamp |-> reg.stamp, plane |-> f]]
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![c] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, corridor>>

\* Admission writes back the count the controller read, plus one.
Admit(c) ==
  /\ Swappable(c)
  /\ reg' = [seats |-> scratch[c].seen + 1, stamp |-> reg.stamp + 1]
  /\ corridor' = corridor \cup {scratch[c].plane}
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![c] = "clear"]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![c] = Fresh]

Retract(c) ==
  /\ desk[c] = "reading"
  /\ ~Swappable(c)
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![c] = "clear"]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![c] = Fresh]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, corridor>>

Touchdown ==
  /\ corridor # {}
  /\ reg.seats > 0
  /\ reg.stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ \E f \in corridor : corridor' = corridor \ {f}
  /\ reg' = [seats |-> reg.seats - 1, stamp |-> reg.stamp + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, scratch>>

\* A desk can go dark without warning; its scratchpad is lost with it.
GoDark(c) ==
  /\ desk[c] # "dark"
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![c] = "dark"]
  /\ scratch' = [scratch EXCEPT ![c] = Fresh]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, corridor>>

Relieve(c) ==
  /\ desk[c] = "dark"
  /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![c] = "clear"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, corridor, scratch>>

Next == \E c \in Controllers :
  Read(c) \/ Admit(c) \/ Retract(c) \/ Touchdown \/ GoDark(c) \/ Relieve(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The approach corridor never holds more aircraft than it is rated for.
CorridorCapacity == Cardinality(corridor) =< Corridor
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Flights = {ba1, lh2, af3}
  Controllers = {north, south}
  Corridor = 2
  MaxStamp = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CorridorCapacity
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator decides which aircraft may enter the approach corridor. The corridor is rated for a fixed number of aircraft. There is no central lock: every controller desk admits aircraft by compare-and-swap on a single shared register that holds the number of seats currently used together with a stamp that ticks on every successful write.

The state is that shared register, the set of flights currently in the corridor, a status for each controller desk (clear, reading, or dark), and a scratchpad per desk holding the seat count it read, the stamp it read, and the flight it intends to admit.

There are six actions. Read fires at a clear desk: the controller copies the register's seat count and stamp onto its scratchpad together with some flight it wants to admit, and the desk goes to reading. A reading desk is swappable when the stamp on its scratchpad still equals the register's live stamp, the seat count it read is below the corridor rating, the flight it names is not already in the corridor, and the register has not reached its final stamp. Admit fires on a swappable desk: the register is rewritten to the seat count the controller read plus one with the stamp advanced, the named flight joins the corridor, and the desk returns to clear with a fresh scratchpad. Retract fires on a reading desk that is not swappable: the desk gives up, clears its scratchpad, and returns to clear. Touchdown removes some flight from the corridor and decrements the register's seat count with the stamp advanced. GoDark models a desk failing silently: the desk goes dark and its scratchpad is lost with it, with nothing announced to the other desks. Relieve brings a dark desk back to clear.

The corridor rating is a hard physical limit on how many aircraft may be flying the approach at once. The stamp check inside the compare-and-swap is the only thing stopping two desks that both read the same seat count from each admitting an aircraft against it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of flights in the approach corridor never exceeds the corridor's rated capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m3p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* Hubs elect a coordinator per epoch; the reign table remembers who held
\* the role in each epoch.  Only a hub whose own view is the live epoch and
\* who actually reigns there may cut a guest code into the audit trail.
CONSTANTS Hubs, MaxEpoch, MaxCodes

Nobody == "nobody"

VARIABLES epoch, view, reign, trail, allowance
vars == <<epoch, view, reign, trail, allowance>>

Boss == reign[epoch]

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ view \in [Hubs -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ reign \in [0..MaxEpoch -> Hubs \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ trail \in Seq([by: Hubs, ep: 0..MaxEpoch])
  /\ allowance \in 0..MaxCodes

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ view = [h \in Hubs |-> 0]
  /\ reign = [e \in 0..MaxEpoch |-> IF e = 0 THEN CHOOSE h \in Hubs : TRUE
                                             ELSE Nobody]
  /\ trail = <<>>
  /\ allowance = MaxCodes

\* Failover: a fresh epoch opens and some hub takes the role in it.
Failover ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E h \in Hubs :
       /\ reign' = [reign EXCEPT ![epoch + 1] = h]
       /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![h] = epoch + 1]
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<trail, allowance>>

\* A lagging hub learns the live epoch.
Catchup ==
  /\ \E h \in Hubs :
       /\ view[h] < epoch
       /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![h] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reign, trail, allowance>>

CutCode ==
  /\ \E h \in Hubs :
       /\ h = Boss
       /\ view[h] = epoch
       /\ Len(trail) < allowance
       /\ trail' = Append(trail, [by |-> h, ep |-> epoch])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, reign, allowance>>

ExpireCode ==
  /\ trail # <<>>
  /\ trail' = Tail(trail)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, reign, allowance>>

\* The householder re-rates how many guest codes may be live at once, and
\* may rate it below the number already cut.
Rerate ==
  /\ \E n \in 0..MaxCodes :
       /\ n # allowance
       /\ allowance' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, view, reign, trail>>

Next == Failover \/ Catchup \/ CutCode \/ ExpireCode \/ Rerate

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Catchup)

\* Every guest code in the audit trail was cut by exactly the hub that
\* reigned in the epoch stamped on it -- no stale or unelected hub ever
\* managed to write one.
NoStaleAuthor == \A i \in 1..Len(trail) : trail[i].by = reign[trail[i].ep]

AllHubsCatchUp == \A h \in Hubs : (view[h] < epoch) ~> (view[h] = epoch)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Hubs = {porch, garage}
  MaxEpoch = 2
  MaxCodes = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleAuthor

PROPERTY AllHubsCatchUp
nl:
A smart-home door lock network lets the household cut temporary guest codes. Only one hub at a time is entitled to cut them: the hubs run a failover election, and every election round opens a new epoch. The network keeps a reign table that records, for each epoch, which hub held the role during it. Each hub also carries its own view of what epoch it believes is live; a hub that missed an election lags behind.

The number of guest codes that may be live at once is not fixed. The householder can re-rate that allowance at any moment while the system runs, including to a number below the count of codes already cut.

The state is the live epoch, the per-hub view of the epoch, the reign table, the audit trail of cut codes (each entry recording the hub that cut it and the epoch stamped on it), and the current allowance.

There are five actions. Failover opens the next epoch, writes some hub into the reign table for that epoch, sets that hub's own view to the new epoch, and advances the live epoch, up to a fixed ceiling of epochs. Catchup takes any hub whose view lags the live epoch and moves its view up to the live epoch. CutCode fires for a hub that both reigns in the live epoch and whose own view equals the live epoch, provided the trail is shorter than the current allowance: an entry recording that hub and the live epoch is appended to the audit trail. ExpireCode drops the oldest entry off the front of the audit trail. Rerate is the householder changing the allowance to any different value between zero and the ceiling.

An unelected hub, or a hub still operating on a stale view of who is in charge, must never manage to get a code into the audit trail. The reign table is the ground truth against which every trail entry can be checked after the fact.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the audit trail names as its author exactly the hub that the reign table records as holding the coordinator role in the epoch stamped on that entry, so no stale or unelected hub ever cuts a guest code.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every hub whose view of the epoch has fallen behind the live epoch eventually catches up to the live epoch.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m6p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* Each track block is handed out as a timed lease.  A train that is merely
\* slow keeps its block: the interlocking refuses to let the clock retire a
\* lease while the block is still physically occupied.
CONSTANTS Blocks, Trains, Term, Horizon

Outside == "outside"
Unheld == "unheld"

VARIABLES pos, claim, lease, clock
vars == <<pos, claim, lease, clock>>

Until == IF clock + Term < Horizon THEN clock + Term ELSE Horizon

TypeOK ==
  /\ pos \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {Outside}]
  /\ claim \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {Outside}]
  /\ lease \in [Blocks -> [holder: Trains \cup {Unheld}, until: 0..Horizon]]
  /\ clock \in 0..Horizon

Init ==
  /\ pos = [t \in Trains |-> Outside]
  /\ claim = [t \in Trains |-> Outside]
  /\ lease = [b \in Blocks |-> [holder |-> Unheld, until |-> 0]]
  /\ clock = 0

Clear(b) == \A t \in Trains : pos[t] # b
Grantable(b) == Clear(b) /\ (lease[b].holder = Unheld \/ lease[b].until < clock)
Valid(t, b) == lease[b].holder = t /\ lease[b].until >= clock
Settled(t) == IF pos[t] = Outside THEN TRUE ELSE lease[pos[t]].until > clock

\* The signalling centre grants a timed lease on an empty, unleased block.
Request(t) ==
  /\ pos[t] = Outside /\ claim[t] = Outside
  /\ \E b \in Blocks :
       /\ Grantable(b)
       /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![b] = [holder |-> t, until |-> Until]]
       /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, clock>>

Enter(t) ==
  /\ claim[t] # Outside
  /\ Valid(t, claim[t])
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = claim[t]]
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![t] = Outside]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock>>

\* A train that dawdled at the signal loses the grant and gives it back.
Forfeit(t) ==
  /\ claim[t] # Outside
  /\ ~Valid(t, claim[t])
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![claim[t]] =
                 IF @.holder = t THEN [holder |-> Unheld, until |-> @.until] ELSE @]
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![t] = Outside]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, clock>>

Extend(t) ==
  /\ pos[t] # Outside
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![pos[t]].until = Until]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, claim, clock>>

Leave(t) ==
  /\ pos[t] # Outside
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![pos[t]] = [holder |-> Unheld, until |-> @.until]]
  /\ pos' = [pos EXCEPT ![t] = Outside]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claim, clock>>

\* Time only moves on while no occupied block's lease would lapse.
Tick ==
  /\ clock < Horizon
  /\ \A t \in Trains : Settled(t)
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pos, claim, lease>>

Next == Tick \/ \E t \in Trains :
  Request(t) \/ Enter(t) \/ Forfeit(t) \/ Extend(t) \/ Leave(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A train sits inside a block only while that block's lease names it and
\* has not lapsed, so two trains never share a block.
BlockExclusion ==
  \A t \in Trains :
    IF pos[t] = Outside THEN TRUE ELSE Valid(t, pos[t])
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Blocks = {nb1, nb2}
  Trains = {tr1, tr2}
  Term = 2
  Horizon = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BlockExclusion
nl:
A subway signalling system divides the line into track blocks. A train may only be inside a block if the signalling centre has granted it a timed lease on that block. The lease carries the name of the train that holds it and a wall-clock deadline after which it lapses. Some trains are simply slow: they take longer than a lease term to clear a block, but they have not failed and their track circuit still shows them present. The interlocking must never retire a lease out from under a train that is physically still there.

The state is each train's physical position (a block or outside), each train's outstanding grant (a block it has been given but not yet entered, or outside), the lease record for each block, and the clock.

There are six actions. Request fires for a train that is neither inside a block nor holding a grant: the signalling centre picks a block that is physically clear and whose lease is either unheld or already lapsed, writes a fresh lease naming that train with a deadline one term ahead (capped at the horizon), and records the grant. Enter moves a train into its granted block, provided the lease on that block still names the train and has not lapsed; the grant is then consumed. Forfeit fires when the train dawdled at the signal and its grant is no longer valid: the grant is dropped and, if the lease still names that train, the lease is handed back as unheld. Extend lets a train that is inside a block push that block's lease deadline forward by another term. Leave takes a train out of its block and hands the lease back as unheld. Tick advances the clock by one, but only while no occupied block's lease deadline is at or behind the new clock reading -- the track circuit veto that stops a slow train from being timed out.

A block is a stretch of live rail. Two trains in the same block is a collision, so the lease is the only thing authorising occupancy.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any train physically inside a block is inside a block whose lease names that very train and whose deadline has not lapsed, so no two trains ever occupy the same block at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m9p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* Theatre block-hours are re-cut in numbered epochs.  Reconfiguration lifts
\* hours out of rooms into a holding pool and lays them back down; the total
\* number of block-hours in the hospital must never change.
CONSTANTS Rooms, Blocks, RoomCap, MaxEpoch, MaxLift, MaxOverride

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET r == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[r] + Tally(f, S \ {r})

VARIABLES hours, holding, epoch, stage, lifted, override
vars == <<hours, holding, epoch, stage, lifted, override>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ hours \in [Rooms -> 0..RoomCap]
  /\ holding \in 0..Blocks
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ stage \in {"steady", "recutting"}
  /\ lifted \in 0..MaxLift
  /\ override \in 0..MaxOverride

Anchor == CHOOSE r \in Rooms : TRUE

Init ==
  /\ hours = [r \in Rooms |-> IF r = Anchor THEN Blocks ELSE 0]
  /\ holding = 0
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ stage = "steady"
  /\ lifted = 0
  /\ override = MaxOverride

\* Opening a new epoch invalidates the previous cut of the theatre day.
OpenEpoch ==
  /\ stage = "steady"
  /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxEpoch THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
  /\ stage' = "recutting"
  /\ lifted' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hours, holding, override>>

Lift ==
  /\ stage = "recutting"
  /\ lifted < MaxLift
  /\ \E r \in Rooms :
       /\ hours[r] > 0
       /\ hours' = [hours EXCEPT ![r] = @ - 1]
  /\ holding' = holding + 1
  /\ lifted' = lifted + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage, override>>

LayDown ==
  /\ stage = "recutting"
  /\ holding > 0
  /\ \E r \in Rooms :
       /\ hours[r] < RoomCap
       /\ hours' = [hours EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
  /\ holding' = holding - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage, lifted, override>>

CloseEpoch ==
  /\ stage = "recutting"
  /\ holding = 0
  /\ stage' = "steady"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hours, holding, epoch, lifted, override>>

\* The chief of surgery can dump the whole holding pool into one room and
\* declare the recut finished, skipping the orderly lay-down.
ChiefOverride ==
  /\ stage = "recutting"
  /\ override > 0
  /\ \E r \in Rooms :
       /\ hours[r] + holding =< RoomCap
       /\ hours' = [hours EXCEPT ![r] = @ + holding]
  /\ holding' = 0
  /\ stage' = "steady"
  /\ override' = override - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, lifted>>

Next == OpenEpoch \/ Lift \/ LayDown \/ CloseEpoch \/ ChiefOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(LayDown) /\ WF_vars(CloseEpoch)

\* Block-hours are conserved: whatever is not sitting in a room is sitting
\* in the holding pool, and the two always add to the day's total.
HourConservation == Tally(hours, Rooms) + holding = Blocks

RecutAlwaysCloses == (stage = "recutting") ~> (stage = "steady")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Rooms = {orA, orB}
  Blocks = 3
  RoomCap = 3
  MaxEpoch = 2
  MaxLift = 2
  MaxOverride = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT HourConservation

PROPERTY RecutAlwaysCloses
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler owns a fixed number of theatre block-hours for the day and distributes them across the operating rooms. The distribution is not edited in place. Instead the scheduler re-cuts the day in numbered epochs: opening a new epoch puts the hospital into a recutting stage, during which block-hours are lifted out of rooms into a holding pool and then laid back down into rooms, after which the epoch closes and the hospital returns to steady stage.

The state is the block-hours currently assigned to each room, the holding pool, the epoch number, the stage (steady or recutting), a counter of how many hours have been lifted in the current epoch, and the number of remaining chief-of-surgery overrides.

There are five actions. OpenEpoch fires in the steady stage: the epoch number advances (saturating at a ceiling), the stage becomes recutting, and the lift counter resets to zero. Lift fires during recutting while the lift counter is below its per-epoch limit: one block-hour leaves some room that has at least one and enters the holding pool, and the lift counter advances. LayDown fires during recutting while the holding pool is non-empty: one block-hour leaves the pool and enters some room that is below its room cap. CloseEpoch fires during recutting once the holding pool is empty and returns the hospital to steady stage. ChiefOverride is a privileged action with a limited number of uses: the chief of surgery dumps the entire holding pool into a single room that can absorb it and declares the recut finished immediately, skipping the orderly lay-down.

Block-hours are the scarce thing being scheduled. Re-cutting the day must move them around; it must never invent an extra hour of theatre time nor quietly lose one in the holding pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The block-hours assigned across all operating rooms plus the block-hours sitting in the holding pool always add up to exactly the hospital's total for the day, so no theatre time is ever created or destroyed by a reconfiguration.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every recutting stage the scheduler enters eventually returns the hospital to the steady stage.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m4p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* Stowage amendments are numbered as they are admitted and must land in
\* the bay plan in that same order.  One planner is merely slow: it can hold
\* an amendment across many ticks, but it never loses it.
CONSTANTS MaxAdmit, Belt, MaxDwell

Nothing == 0

VARIABLES booked, belt, plan, inHand, dwell, alarm
vars == <<booked, belt, plan, inHand, dwell, alarm>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ booked \in Seq(1..MaxAdmit)
  /\ belt \in Seq(1..MaxAdmit)
  /\ plan \in Seq(1..MaxAdmit)
  /\ inHand \in 0..MaxAdmit
  /\ dwell \in 0..MaxDwell
  /\ alarm \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ booked = <<>>
  /\ belt = <<>>
  /\ plan = <<>>
  /\ inHand = Nothing
  /\ dwell = 0
  /\ alarm = FALSE

\* Backpressure: nothing is booked while the belt is at its depth limit.
Book ==
  /\ Len(belt) < Belt
  /\ Len(booked) < MaxAdmit
  /\ booked' = Append(booked, Len(booked) + 1)
  /\ belt' = Append(belt, Len(booked) + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, inHand, dwell, alarm>>

Grab ==
  /\ inHand = Nothing
  /\ belt # <<>>
  /\ inHand' = Head(belt)
  /\ belt' = Tail(belt)
  /\ dwell' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, plan, alarm>>

\* The slow planner sits on the amendment without dropping it.
Dawdle ==
  /\ inHand # Nothing
  /\ dwell < MaxDwell
  /\ dwell' = dwell + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, belt, plan, inHand, alarm>>

Merge ==
  /\ inHand # Nothing
  /\ plan' = Append(plan, inHand)
  /\ inHand' = Nothing
  /\ dwell' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, belt, alarm>>

\* The yard raises or drops its congestion light when intake is blocked.
Congestion ==
  /\ Len(belt) = Belt \/ Len(booked) = MaxAdmit
  /\ alarm' = ~alarm
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, belt, plan, inHand, dwell>>

Next == Book \/ Grab \/ Dawdle \/ Merge \/ Congestion

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The amendments already merged into the bay plan are exactly the opening
\* run of the booked amendments, in booking order: nothing was skipped,
\* reordered, or dropped on the way through the slow planner.
NoLostAmendment == SubSeq(booked, 1, Len(plan)) = plan
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  MaxAdmit = 3
  Belt = 2
  MaxDwell = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoLostAmendment
nl:
A container-ship crane yard maintains one shared bay stowage plan. Amendments to that plan are not written directly. Each amendment is booked with the next sequential number and placed on an intake belt of bounded depth; a single planner takes amendments off the belt one at a time and merges them into the bay plan. Because the belt is bounded, nothing new is booked while the belt is at its depth limit -- that is the backpressure. The planner in this yard is slow but reliable: it can sit on an amendment across many ticks without ever dropping it.

The state is the sequence of booked amendment numbers, the intake belt, the bay plan (the sequence of amendments actually merged), the amendment currently in the planner's hand (or nothing), how long the planner has been dwelling on it, and a congestion light.

There are five actions. Book fires when the belt is below its depth limit and the yard has not exhausted its amendment budget: the next sequential amendment number is appended both to the booked list and to the tail of the belt. Grab fires when the planner's hands are empty and the belt is non-empty: the head of the belt moves into the planner's hand, the belt advances, and the dwell counter resets. Dawdle fires while the planner holds an amendment and its dwell counter is below the dwell limit: the counter simply advances and nothing else moves, which is how a slow-but-not-failed planner is modelled. Merge fires while the planner holds an amendment: that amendment is appended to the bay plan, the hand is emptied, and the dwell counter resets. Congestion fires whenever intake is blocked -- either the belt is at its depth limit or the amendment budget is exhausted -- and simply toggles the yard's congestion light.

The bay plan is the shared record. An amendment that was booked but never reached the plan, or one that reached the plan out of order, is a lost update: the physical stow would no longer match the paperwork.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bay plan is always exactly the opening run of the booked amendment list, in booking order, so no booked amendment is ever skipped, reordered, or dropped on its way through the slow planner.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m6p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

\* Two independent tower facilities share one runway pool.  A timed lease on
\* a runway is what entitles a tower to arm and then blow that runway's
\* arrestor charge -- a charge that exists exactly once.
CONSTANTS North, South, Runways, Term, Horizon, MaxSorties

Towers == North \cup South
Sides == {"north", "south"}
SideOf(w) == IF w \in North THEN "north" ELSE "south"
Unheld == "unheld"
NoJob == "nojob"

VARIABLES lease, barrel, pyro, job, sorties, clock
vars == <<lease, barrel, pyro, job, sorties, clock>>

Deadline == IF clock + Term < Horizon THEN clock + Term ELSE Horizon

TypeOK ==
  /\ lease \in [Runways -> [holder: Towers \cup {Unheld}, until: 0..Horizon]]
  /\ barrel \in [Runways -> {"cold", "armed", "spent"}]
  /\ pyro \in [Runways -> Int]
  /\ job \in [Towers -> Runways \cup {NoJob}]
  /\ sorties \in [Sides -> 0..MaxSorties]
  /\ clock \in 0..Horizon

Init ==
  /\ lease = [r \in Runways |-> [holder |-> Unheld, until |-> 0]]
  /\ barrel = [r \in Runways |-> "cold"]
  /\ pyro = [r \in Runways |-> 1]
  /\ job = [w \in Towers |-> NoJob]
  /\ sorties = [s \in Sides |-> 0]
  /\ clock = 0

Live(w, r) == lease[r].holder = w /\ lease[r].until >= clock

Take(w) ==
  /\ job[w] = NoJob
  /\ sorties[SideOf(w)] < MaxSorties
  /\ \E r \in Runways :
       /\ lease[r].holder = Unheld \/ lease[r].until < clock
       /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![r] = [holder |-> w, until |-> Deadline]]
       /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![w] = r]
  /\ sorties' = [sorties EXCEPT ![SideOf(w)] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<barrel, pyro, clock>>

Arm(w) ==
  /\ job[w] # NoJob
  /\ Live(w, job[w])
  /\ barrel[job[w]] = "cold"
  /\ barrel' = [barrel EXCEPT ![job[w]] = "armed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, pyro, job, sorties, clock>>

\* The one irreversible step: the charge is consumed and cannot be reloaded.
Blow(w) ==
  /\ job[w] # NoJob
  /\ Live(w, job[w])
  /\ barrel[job[w]] = "armed"
  /\ pyro[job[w]] > 0
  /\ barrel' = [barrel EXCEPT ![job[w]] = "spent"]
  /\ pyro' = [pyro EXCEPT ![job[w]] = @ - 1]
  /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![w] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, sorties, clock>>

Handback(w) ==
  /\ job[w] # NoJob
  /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![job[w]] =
                 IF @.holder = w THEN [holder |-> Unheld, until |-> @.until] ELSE @]
  /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![w] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<barrel, pyro, sorties, clock>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock' = IF clock < Horizon THEN clock + 1 ELSE clock
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, barrel, pyro, job, sorties>>

Finish == \E w \in Towers : Blow(w) \/ Handback(w)
Next == Tick \/ Finish \/ (\E w \in Towers : Take(w) \/ Arm(w))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Finish)

\* A runway reads as spent exactly when its arrestor charge is gone, so the
\* charge can be blown once and never a second time.
SingleShot == \A r \in Runways : (barrel[r] = "spent") <=> (pyro[r] = 0)

EveryJobCloses == \A w \in Towers : (job[w] # NoJob) ~> (job[w] = NoJob)
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator is operated by two independent tower facilities, North and South, that draw from one shared pool of runways -- neither facility owns runways of its own. Each runway carries an arrestor barrel loaded with exactly one pyrotechnic charge. Blowing that charge rigs the barrier for an emergency landing and is completely irreversible: the charge cannot be reloaded in service.

A tower is only entitled to touch a runway's barrel while it holds a timed lease on that runway. The lease names the holding tower and a deadline; past the deadline it is dead and the runway can be leased to the other facility.

The state is the lease record for each runway, the barrel state for each runway (cold, armed, or spent), the number of charges left in each barrel, the runway each tower is currently working (or none), a per-facility sortie budget, and the clock.

There are five actions. Take fires for a tower with no current job and remaining sortie budget: it picks a runway whose lease is unheld or already past its deadline, writes a fresh lease naming itself with a deadline one term ahead capped at the horizon, records the runway as its job, and spends one sortie. Arm fires while a tower holds a live lease on its job runway and that barrel is cold: the barrel moves to armed. Blow is the irreversible step: with a live lease, an armed barrel, and a charge still loaded, the barrel is marked spent, one charge is consumed, and the tower's job closes. Handback closes a tower's job unconditionally, returning the lease to unheld if that lease still names this tower. Tick advances the clock by one, saturating at the horizon.

The pyrotechnic charge is real hardware. Two facilities each blowing the same runway's barrel would be a double firing on a runway that only ever carried one charge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A runway's barrel reads as spent exactly when its charge count has reached zero, so the irreversible firing of a runway's arrestor charge happens at most once no matter how the two facilities race for its lease.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every tower that takes on a runway job eventually closes that job, whether by blowing the charge or by handing the lease back.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m9p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

\* Matchmaker nodes stage roster edits stamped with the shard epoch.  A recut
\* of the shards bumps the epoch and invalidates every staged edit, so the
\* lobby roster stays the exact replay of its own journal.
CONSTANTS Players, Nodes, MaxEpoch, MaxSeats, Journal

Quiet == "quiet"

VARIABLES roster, ledger, epoch, seats, staged
vars == <<roster, ledger, epoch, seats, staged>>

Blank == [kind |-> Quiet, who |-> CHOOSE p \in Players : TRUE, ep |-> 0]

RECURSIVE Replay(_)
Replay(n) ==
  IF n = 0 THEN {}
  ELSE LET before == Replay(n - 1)
           e == ledger[n]
       IN IF e.kind = "join" THEN before \cup {e.who} ELSE before \ {e.who}

TypeOK ==
  /\ roster \subseteq Players
  /\ ledger \in Seq([kind: {"join", "leave"}, who: Players])
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ seats \in 0..MaxSeats
  /\ staged \in [Nodes -> [kind: {Quiet, "join", "leave"}, who: Players,
                           ep: 0..MaxEpoch]]

Init ==
  /\ roster = {}
  /\ ledger = <<>>
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ seats = MaxSeats
  /\ staged = [n \in Nodes |-> Blank]

Ready(n) ==
  /\ staged[n].kind # Quiet
  /\ staged[n].ep = epoch
  /\ Len(ledger) < Journal
  /\ IF staged[n].kind = "join"
       THEN staged[n].who \notin roster /\ Cardinality(roster) < seats
       ELSE staged[n].who \in roster

Stage(n) ==
  /\ staged[n].kind = Quiet
  /\ \E k \in {"join", "leave"}, p \in Players :
       staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![n] = [kind |-> k, who |-> p, ep |-> epoch]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, ledger, epoch, seats>>

\* Committing writes the roster and the journal in one step.
Commit(n) ==
  /\ Ready(n)
  /\ roster' = IF staged[n].kind = "join"
                 THEN roster \cup {staged[n].who}
                 ELSE roster \ {staged[n].who}
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, [kind |-> staged[n].kind, who |-> staged[n].who])
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![n] = Blank]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, seats>>

Drop(n) ==
  /\ staged[n].kind # Quiet
  /\ ~Ready(n)
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![n] = Blank]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, ledger, epoch, seats>>

\* A shard recut opens a new epoch; edits staged under the old one are stale.
Recut ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, ledger, seats, staged>>

\* Operators resize the lobby while players are already in it.
Resize ==
  /\ \E n \in 0..MaxSeats : n # seats /\ seats' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, ledger, epoch, staged>>

Next == Recut \/ Resize \/ \E n \in Nodes : Stage(n) \/ Commit(n) \/ Drop(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The live roster is exactly what you get by replaying the journal from
\* empty, so no accepted edit was ever overwritten or lost between nodes.
RosterReplays == roster = Replay(Len(ledger))
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Players = {pa, pb}
  Nodes = {mm1, mm2}
  MaxEpoch = 1
  MaxSeats = 2
  Journal = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RosterReplays
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker keeps one shared lobby roster. Several matchmaker nodes edit that roster, but never in place: a node first stages an edit -- a join or a leave naming some player -- stamped with the shard epoch that was live when it staged. Shard layout is periodically recut, which opens a new epoch; any edit still staged under an older epoch is stale and can no longer be committed. Alongside the roster the matchmaker keeps a journal of every edit it accepted, in acceptance order. The lobby's seat count is not fixed either: operators resize the lobby at runtime, including downward while players are already seated.

The state is the live roster, the journal, the epoch, the seat count, and one staging slot per node holding a kind (quiet, join, or leave), a player, and the epoch stamp.

There are five actions. Stage fires for a node with a quiet slot: it writes some join or leave for some player into its slot, stamped with the live epoch. A staged edit is ready when its kind is not quiet, its epoch stamp still equals the live epoch, the journal has room, and the edit actually applies -- a join needs the player absent from the roster and the roster below the current seat count, a leave needs the player present. Commit fires on a ready edit and performs the roster change and the journal append as one indivisible step, then blanks the node's slot. Drop fires on a staged edit that is not ready and simply blanks the slot. Recut advances the epoch, up to a ceiling, which strands every edit staged under the previous epoch. Resize sets the seat count to any different value between zero and the maximum, whether or not the roster currently fits.

The journal is the authority on what the matchmaker agreed to. If a node's edit changed the roster without landing in the journal, or landed in the journal without changing the roster, or clobbered another node's concurrent edit, the roster would drift away from its own history.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The live roster is always exactly the set you obtain by replaying the journal from the empty roster, applying each recorded join and leave in order, so no accepted edit is ever lost or overwritten.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m7p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* One compare-and-swap register decides which hub owns the front-door bolt.
\* The bolt's event tape records every take and every give-back; if two hubs
\* ever held the bolt together the tape would show two takes in a row.
CONSTANTS Hubs, MaxTry, TapeLen, MaxFaults

Free == "free"

VARIABLES reg, mode, tape, tries, faults
vars == <<reg, mode, tape, tries, faults>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in Hubs \cup {Free}
  /\ mode \in [Hubs -> {"idle", "trying", "driving", "dead"}]
  /\ tape \in Seq([by: Hubs, kind: {"take", "back"}])
  /\ tries \in [Hubs -> 0..MaxTry]
  /\ faults \in 0..MaxFaults

Init ==
  /\ reg = Free
  /\ mode = [h \in Hubs |-> "idle"]
  /\ tape = <<>>
  /\ tries = [h \in Hubs |-> 0]
  /\ faults = 0

CanTake(h) == mode[h] = "trying" /\ reg = Free /\ Len(tape) + 2 =< TapeLen

Attempt(h) ==
  /\ mode[h] = "idle" /\ tries[h] < MaxTry
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![h] = "trying"]
  /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![h] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tape, faults>>

\* The swap succeeds only against a register still reading free.
Take(h) ==
  /\ CanTake(h)
  /\ reg' = h
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![h] = "driving"]
  /\ tape' = Append(tape, [by |-> h, kind |-> "take"])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, faults>>

Yield(h) ==
  /\ mode[h] = "trying" /\ ~CanTake(h)
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tape, tries, faults>>

Give(h) ==
  /\ mode[h] = "driving"
  /\ reg' = Free
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
  /\ tape' = Append(tape, [by |-> h, kind |-> "back"])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, faults>>

\* A hub can drop off the mesh mid-hold with nothing announced.
Fault(h) ==
  /\ mode[h] \in {"trying", "driving"} /\ faults < MaxFaults
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![h] = "dead"]
  /\ faults' = faults + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tape, tries>>

\* The watchdog swaps the dead owner out and closes its tape entry.
Evict(h) ==
  /\ mode[h] = "dead" /\ reg = h
  /\ reg' = Free
  /\ tape' = Append(tape, [by |-> h, kind |-> "back"])
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, tries, faults>>

Rejoin(h) ==
  /\ mode[h] = "dead" /\ reg # h
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, tape, tries, faults>>

Quiet == (\A h \in Hubs : mode[h] = "idle" /\ tries[h] = MaxTry) /\ UNCHANGED vars

Resolve == \E h \in Hubs : Take(h) \/ Yield(h)
Next == Resolve \/ Quiet \/
        \E h \in Hubs : Attempt(h) \/ Give(h) \/ Fault(h) \/ Evict(h) \/ Rejoin(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Resolve)

\* The bolt's event tape strictly alternates: odd entries are takes, and
\* every even entry gives the bolt back on behalf of the hub that just took
\* it.  Two hubs holding the bolt at once would break that alternation.
BoltTapeAlternates ==
  \A i \in 1..Len(tape) :
    IF i % 2 = 1 THEN tape[i].kind = "take"
                 ELSE tape[i].kind = "back" /\ tape[i].by = tape[i - 1].by

TryingResolves == \A h \in Hubs : (mode[h] = "trying") ~> (mode[h] # "trying")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Hubs = {porch, patio}
  MaxTry = 2
  TapeLen = 4
  MaxFaults = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BoltTapeAlternates

PROPERTY TryingResolves
nl:
A smart-home door lock network arbitrates the front-door bolt through a single compare-and-swap register. The register reads either free or the name of the hub that currently owns the bolt; a hub takes the bolt only by swapping the register from free to itself. Alongside the register the lock keeps an event tape: every time a hub takes the bolt an entry is appended, and every time the bolt is handed back another entry is appended naming the same hub.

The state is the register, a mode for each hub (idle, trying, driving, or dead), the event tape, a per-hub attempt allowance, and a fault budget.

There are eight actions. Attempt moves an idle hub with allowance left into trying and spends one attempt. A trying hub can take the bolt when the register reads free and the tape still has room for both a take and its matching give-back. Take performs the swap: the register is written with the hub's name, the hub becomes driving, and a take entry is appended. Yield fires for a trying hub that cannot take the bolt right now and simply returns it to idle. Give fires for a driving hub: the register goes back to free, a give-back entry naming that hub is appended, and the hub returns to idle. Fault models a hub dropping off the mesh with nothing announced -- a trying or driving hub silently becomes dead, spending one unit of the fault budget, and the register is left exactly as it was. Evict is the watchdog: when the register still names a dead hub, the watchdog swaps it back to free and appends the give-back entry on the dead hub's behalf. Rejoin brings a dead hub the register no longer names back to idle. Quiet applies only when every hub is idle with its attempt allowance spent, and leaves the network exactly as it stands.

The bolt is one motor. The event tape is the audit record of who had it and when, and it is only coherent if holds never overlap.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bolt's event tape strictly alternates -- every odd-numbered entry is a take, and every even-numbered entry is a give-back naming the same hub as the take immediately before it -- so two hubs never hold the bolt at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every hub that starts trying for the bolt eventually stops trying, either by taking the bolt or by yielding.
