---- MODULE W4Od18m0p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Hubs edit the shared auto-lock profile optimistically: read the whole
\* profile plus its version, then post a write.  Posts sit in an unordered
\* radio buffer, so a write can land long after the profile has moved on.
CONSTANTS Hubs, Rules, MaxVer, Buffer, MaxRetry, MaxDrop

Unset == "unset"

VARIABLES profile, posts, landed, retry, dropped
vars == <<profile, posts, landed, retry, dropped>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ profile \in [mix: SUBSET Rules, ver: 0..MaxVer]
  /\ posts \subseteq [by: Hubs, base: 0..MaxVer, saw: SUBSET Rules, add: Rules]
  /\ landed \in [Hubs -> Rules \cup {Unset}]
  /\ retry \in [Hubs -> 0..MaxRetry]
  /\ dropped \in 0..MaxDrop

Init ==
  /\ profile = [mix |-> {}, ver |-> 0]
  /\ posts = {}
  /\ landed = [h \in Hubs |-> Unset]
  /\ retry = [h \in Hubs |-> 0]
  /\ dropped = 0

Current(m) == m.base = profile.ver /\ profile.ver < MaxVer

\* A hub reads the whole profile and posts a write built on that reading.
Compose(h) ==
  /\ Cardinality(posts) < Buffer
  /\ ~(\E m \in posts : m.by = h)
  /\ \E r \in Rules :
       posts' = posts \cup {[by |-> h, base |-> profile.ver,
                             saw |-> profile.mix, add |-> r]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<profile, landed, retry, dropped>>

\* The write installs the reading it was built on, plus its own rule.  That
\* is why a write built on a stale reading would erase somebody's rule.
Install ==
  /\ \E m \in posts :
       /\ Current(m)
       /\ profile' = [mix |-> m.saw \cup {m.add}, ver |-> profile.ver + 1]
       /\ landed' = [landed EXCEPT ![m.by] = m.add]
       /\ posts' = posts \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<retry, dropped>>

Bounce ==
  /\ \E m \in posts :
       /\ ~Current(m)
       /\ retry[m.by] < MaxRetry
       /\ retry' = [retry EXCEPT ![m.by] = @ + 1]
       /\ posts' = posts \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<profile, landed, dropped>>

Abandon ==
  /\ \E m \in posts :
       /\ ~Current(m)
       /\ retry[m.by] = MaxRetry
       /\ posts' = posts \ {m}
  /\ dropped' = IF dropped < MaxDrop THEN dropped + 1 ELSE dropped
  /\ UNCHANGED <<profile, landed, retry>>

Next == (\E h \in Hubs : Compose(h)) \/ Install \/ Bounce \/ Abandon

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whatever rule a hub got into the profile is still in the profile: no
\* later write ever quietly erased an earlier hub's accepted edit.
NoErasedRule ==
  \A h \in Hubs : landed[h] = Unset \/ landed[h] \in profile.mix
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Hubs = {hallway, garage}
  Rules = {nightlock, awaylock}
  MaxVer = 2
  Buffer = 2
  MaxRetry = 1
  MaxDrop = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoErasedRule
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps a single shared auto-lock profile: a set of rules together with a version number. Hubs do not lock the profile before editing it. Each hub reads the entire profile -- both the rule set it sees and the version stamped on it -- and then posts a write that carries that reading plus one new rule it wants added. The posts sit in an unordered radio buffer of bounded size, so a write may be delivered long after the profile has moved on under it.

The state is the profile, the buffer of posted writes, a record of the rule each hub last got accepted, a per-hub retry counter, and a counter of abandoned writes.

A posted write is current when the version it was built on still equals the profile's live version and the profile has not reached its final version.

There are four actions. Compose fires for a hub that has no post outstanding while the buffer has room: the hub snapshots the profile's rule set and version and posts a write adding some rule. Install takes any current post out of the buffer and writes the profile back as the rule set that post saw plus that post's own rule, with the version advanced by one, and records the added rule as that hub's accepted edit. That write-back is the whole point: a write installs the reading it was built on, so a write built on a stale reading would silently erase every rule accepted in between. Bounce takes a post that is no longer current out of the buffer while its author still has retry allowance and spends one retry. Abandon takes a non-current post out of the buffer when its author's retry allowance is spent and tallies an abandoned write, saturating at the ceiling.

The version check on Install is the only defence. Without it, two hubs that read the same profile would each install their own snapshot and the second would wipe out the first hub's rule.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every rule that a hub has had accepted into the shared auto-lock profile is still present in that profile, so no accepted edit is ever quietly erased by a later write.

---- MODULE W4Od11m9p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Spooled jobs are re-homed between printers in numbered epochs: drain the
\* trays into a crate, then fill the trays back up.  The per-tray limit is
\* re-tuned by the operator while all this is going on.
CONSTANTS Jobs, Printers, MaxEpoch, MaxCap

VARIABLES tray, crate, bin, epoch, stage, cap
vars == <<tray, crate, bin, epoch, stage, cap>>

Room == \E p \in Printers : Cardinality(tray[p]) < cap

TypeOK ==
  /\ tray \in [Printers -> SUBSET Jobs]
  /\ crate \subseteq Jobs
  /\ bin \subseteq Jobs
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ stage \in {"spooling", "draining", "filling"}
  /\ cap \in 1..MaxCap

Anchor == CHOOSE p \in Printers : TRUE

Init ==
  /\ tray = [p \in Printers |-> IF p = Anchor THEN Jobs ELSE {}]
  /\ crate = {}
  /\ bin = {}
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ stage = "spooling"
  /\ cap = MaxCap

OpenEpoch ==
  /\ stage = "spooling"
  /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxEpoch THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
  /\ stage' = "draining"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tray, crate, bin, cap>>

\* Draining only ever lifts jobs out of trays into the crate.
Lift ==
  /\ stage = "draining"
  /\ \E p \in Printers : \E j \in tray[p] :
       /\ tray' = [tray EXCEPT ![p] = @ \ {j}]
       /\ crate' = crate \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, epoch, stage, cap>>

Turn ==
  /\ stage = "draining"
  /\ stage' = "filling"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tray, crate, bin, epoch, cap>>

\* Filling only ever empties the crate: into a tray with room under the
\* current limit, or, if no tray has room, into the discard bin.
Drain ==
  /\ stage = "filling"
  /\ \E j \in crate :
       /\ crate' = crate \ {j}
       /\ \/ /\ Room
             /\ \E p \in Printers :
                  /\ Cardinality(tray[p]) < cap
                  /\ tray' = [tray EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {j}]
             /\ bin' = bin
          \/ /\ ~Room
             /\ tray' = tray
             /\ bin' = bin \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage, cap>>

CloseEpoch ==
  /\ stage = "filling"
  /\ crate = {}
  /\ stage' = "spooling"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tray, crate, bin, epoch, cap>>

Print ==
  /\ stage = "spooling"
  /\ \E p \in Printers : \E j \in tray[p] :
       /\ tray' = [tray EXCEPT ![p] = @ \ {j}]
       /\ bin' = bin \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crate, epoch, stage, cap>>

\* The operator re-tunes the per-tray limit at any moment.
Retune ==
  /\ \E n \in 1..MaxCap : n # cap /\ cap' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tray, crate, bin, epoch, stage>>

Next == OpenEpoch \/ Lift \/ Turn \/ Drain \/ CloseEpoch \/ Print \/ Retune

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Turn) /\ WF_vars(Drain) /\ WF_vars(CloseEpoch)

\* Every spooled job sits in exactly one place -- one printer's tray, the
\* migration crate, or the discard bin -- so re-homing never duplicates or
\* loses a job.
JobConservation ==
  \A j \in Jobs :
    Cardinality({p \in Printers : j \in tray[p]})
      + (IF j \in crate THEN 1 ELSE 0)
      + (IF j \in bin THEN 1 ELSE 0) = 1

RehomeFinishes == (stage # "spooling") ~> (stage = "spooling")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Jobs = {jb1, jb2, jb3}
  Printers = {pr1, pr2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
  MaxCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT JobConservation

PROPERTY RehomeFinishes
nl:
A print shop spooler holds a fixed set of print jobs and distributes them across several printers. Jobs are not moved between printers ad hoc. Instead the shop re-homes the spool in numbered epochs: opening an epoch puts the shop into a draining stage in which jobs are lifted out of printer trays into a migration crate, then the shop turns to a filling stage in which the crate is emptied back into trays, and finally the epoch closes and the shop returns to spooling. The per-tray job limit is not fixed either -- the operator re-tunes it at any moment, including in the middle of a re-home.

The state is the set of jobs in each printer's tray, the migration crate, the discard bin, the epoch number, the stage, and the current per-tray limit.

There are seven actions. OpenEpoch fires while spooling: the epoch advances, saturating at a ceiling, and the stage becomes draining. Lift fires while draining: one job leaves some printer's tray and enters the crate; draining only ever moves jobs in that direction. Turn ends draining and begins filling. Drain fires while filling: one job leaves the crate and, if any tray is below the current limit, joins such a tray; if no tray has room under the current limit the job goes to the discard bin instead. CloseEpoch fires while filling once the crate is empty and returns the shop to spooling. Print fires while spooling: a job leaves a tray and goes to the discard bin as finished work. Retune sets the per-tray limit to any different value in range, whatever the trays currently hold.

A print job is a physical piece of work. Re-homing may move it and printing may retire it, but nothing in the shop should ever make a second copy of a job or lose one between a tray and the crate.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job in the shop sits in exactly one place at every moment -- in exactly one printer's tray, or in the migration crate, or in the discard bin -- so re-homing never duplicates a job and never loses one.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every re-home the shop starts eventually finishes and returns the shop to the spooling stage.

---- MODULE W4Od16m7p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* One compare-and-swap register decides which station drives the single
\* dispensing head.  Every turn of the head is numbered, and each dose slip
\* records the turn under which it was cut.
CONSTANTS Stations, MaxTurn, MaxDoses, MaxOverride, MaxLock

Idle == "idle"

VARIABLES reg, busy, slips, servedIn, override, lockouts
vars == <<reg, busy, slips, servedIn, override, lockouts>>

CanClaim == reg.holder = Idle /\ reg.turn < MaxTurn

TypeOK ==
  /\ reg \in [holder: Stations \cup {Idle}, turn: 0..MaxTurn]
  /\ busy \subseteq Stations
  /\ slips \in Seq([by: Stations, turn: 1..MaxTurn])
  /\ servedIn \subseteq Stations
  /\ override \in 0..MaxOverride
  /\ lockouts \in 0..MaxLock

Init ==
  /\ reg = [holder |-> Idle, turn |-> 0]
  /\ busy = {}
  /\ slips = <<>>
  /\ servedIn = {}
  /\ override = MaxOverride
  /\ lockouts = 0

\* Swapping the register from idle to a station opens that station's turn.
Claim(s) ==
  /\ CanClaim
  /\ reg' = [holder |-> s, turn |-> reg.turn + 1]
  /\ busy' = {s}
  /\ servedIn' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slips, override, lockouts>>

\* The head is physical: it cuts a dose for whichever station is on it.
Dispense(s) ==
  /\ s \in busy
  /\ s \notin servedIn
  /\ Len(slips) < MaxDoses
  /\ reg.turn > 0
  /\ slips' = Append(slips, [by |-> s, turn |-> reg.turn])
  /\ servedIn' = servedIn \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, busy, override, lockouts>>

Release(s) ==
  /\ s \in busy
  /\ busy' = busy \ {s}
  /\ reg' = [holder |-> Idle, turn |-> reg.turn]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slips, servedIn, override, lockouts>>

\* The duty pharmacist can seize the head from whoever holds it; the seizure
\* opens a fresh turn and drops the incumbent off the head.
Seize(s) ==
  /\ override > 0
  /\ reg.turn < MaxTurn
  /\ reg' = [holder |-> s, turn |-> reg.turn + 1]
  /\ busy' = {s}
  /\ servedIn' = {}
  /\ override' = override - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slips, lockouts>>

\* A station that cannot get the head is told the cabinet is locked out.
Denied ==
  /\ ~CanClaim
  /\ lockouts' = IF lockouts < MaxLock THEN lockouts + 1 ELSE lockouts
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, busy, slips, servedIn, override>>

Next == Denied \/ \E s \in Stations : Claim(s) \/ Dispense(s) \/ Release(s) \/ Seize(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Dose slips carry strictly increasing turn numbers.  Since a turn is opened
\* by exactly one swap of the register, two stations on the head together
\* would cut two slips bearing the same turn.
SlipsAdvance == \A i \in 2..Len(slips) : slips[i].turn > slips[i - 1].turn
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Stations = {intakeA, intakeB}
  MaxTurn = 3
  MaxDoses = 3
  MaxOverride = 1
  MaxLock = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SlipsAdvance
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser has several intake stations that all feed the same single dispensing head. Which station drives the head is decided by one compare-and-swap register holding either idle or a station name, together with a turn number. Swapping the register from idle to a station opens a new, higher-numbered turn for that station. Every dose the head cuts produces a slip recording the station that took it and the turn number that was open at the time.

The state is the register, the set of stations physically on the head, the sequence of dose slips, the set of stations already served in the open turn, the remaining pharmacist overrides, and a lockout tally.

There are five actions. Claim fires when the register reads idle and the turn number has not reached its ceiling: the register is swapped to name the claiming station with the turn advanced by one, that station becomes the only one on the head, and the served set is cleared. Dispense fires for a station that is physically on the head, has not already been served in the open turn, and while the slip book has room: a slip is appended recording that station and the open turn number, and the station is marked served for this turn. Release takes a station off the head and swaps the register back to idle, leaving the turn number where it is. Seize is the duty pharmacist's privileged override: with overrides remaining and the turn number below its ceiling, the pharmacist swaps the register to any station regardless of who holds it, opening a new turn, dropping the incumbent off the head and clearing the served set. Denied fires whenever the head cannot be claimed and simply advances a lockout tally that saturates at its ceiling.

The dispensing head is one motor with one cassette path. Two stations driving it together would interleave two prescriptions into one bottle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The turn numbers recorded on the dose slips are strictly increasing, so no two doses were ever cut under the same turn and therefore no two stations ever drove the dispensing head at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od3m9p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Settlement instructions are debited into an unordered wire pool and
\* credited on arrival, in whatever order they arrive.  A cutover opens a
\* new netting epoch and every instruction from the old one is unwound.
CONSTANTS Banks, Float, MaxEpoch, WireCap, MaxAmt, MaxUnwound

VARIABLES book, wire, epoch, stage, unwound
vars == <<book, wire, epoch, stage, unwound>>

RECURSIVE Ledger(_)
Ledger(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN book[b] + Ledger(S \ {b})

RECURSIVE Pot(_)
Pot(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET m == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN m.amt + Pot(S \ {m})

Stale == {m \in wire : m.ep # epoch}

TypeOK ==
  /\ book \in [Banks -> 0..Float]
  /\ wire \subseteq [id: 1..WireCap, from: Banks, to: Banks,
                     amt: 1..MaxAmt, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ stage \in {"open", "cutover"}
  /\ unwound \in 0..MaxUnwound

Anchor == CHOOSE b \in Banks : TRUE

Init ==
  /\ book = [b \in Banks |-> IF b = Anchor THEN Float ELSE 0]
  /\ wire = {}
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ stage = "open"
  /\ unwound = 0

\* Posting debits the payer immediately; the money now rides the wire.
Post ==
  /\ stage = "open"
  /\ \E i \in 1..WireCap : \E f \in Banks : \E t \in Banks : \E a \in 1..MaxAmt :
       /\ ~(\E m \in wire : m.id = i)
       /\ f # t /\ book[f] >= a
       /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![f] = @ - a]
       /\ wire' = wire \cup {[id |-> i, from |-> f, to |-> t,
                              amt |-> a, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage, unwound>>

\* Instructions arrive in arbitrary order; the pool has no ordering at all.
Credit ==
  /\ \E m \in wire :
       /\ m.ep = epoch
       /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![m.to] = @ + m.amt]
       /\ wire' = wire \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage, unwound>>

Cutover ==
  /\ stage = "open"
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ stage' = "cutover"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, wire, unwound>>

\* Unwinding hands an old-epoch instruction back to the payer intact.
Unwind ==
  /\ stage = "cutover"
  /\ \E m \in Stale :
       /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![m.from] = @ + m.amt]
       /\ wire' = wire \ {m}
  /\ unwound' = IF unwound < MaxUnwound THEN unwound + 1 ELSE unwound
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage>>

Reopen ==
  /\ stage = "cutover"
  /\ Stale = {}
  /\ stage' = "open"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<book, wire, epoch, unwound>>

Next == Post \/ Credit \/ Cutover \/ Unwind \/ Reopen

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Unwind) /\ WF_vars(Reopen)

\* Money is conserved: what sits on the banks' books plus what is riding
\* the wire always adds to the day's float.
FundsConservation == Ledger(Banks) + Pot(wire) = Float

CutoverCompletes == (stage = "cutover") ~> (stage = "open")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Banks = {bkA, bkB}
  Float = 3
  MaxEpoch = 2
  WireCap = 2
  MaxAmt = 2
  MaxUnwound = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT FundsConservation

PROPERTY CutoverCompletes
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch moves money between member banks over a wire. Posting an instruction debits the payer's book immediately; the money then rides the wire until the instruction is credited to the payee. The wire is an unordered pool of bounded size: instructions are delivered in whatever order the network feels like, never in the order they were posted.

The batch is netted in numbered epochs. A cutover advances the epoch and puts the settlement into a cutover stage, in which every instruction still riding the wire is stale -- it belongs to the previous epoch -- and must be unwound back to the payer before the batch can reopen.

The state is each bank's book balance, the wire pool, the epoch number, the stage (open or cutover), and a tally of unwound instructions that saturates at a ceiling.

There are five actions. Post fires while the batch is open and some wire slot number is unused: a payer with sufficient funds is debited by an amount, and an instruction carrying that free slot number, the payer, the payee, the amount, and the current epoch joins the wire. The slot number is what keeps two otherwise-identical instructions distinct, and it bounds how many can ride the wire at once. Credit takes any instruction on the wire whose epoch matches the live epoch, credits the payee by that amount, and removes the instruction from the wire; because the wire is a pool rather than a queue, any pending instruction may be the one chosen. Cutover advances the epoch, up to a ceiling, and moves the batch into the cutover stage. Unwind takes any stale instruction off the wire during cutover and hands its full amount back to the payer, advancing the unwound tally. Reopen returns the batch to the open stage once no stale instruction remains on the wire.

Money is the conserved quantity. A debit that never becomes either a credit or an unwind would be money destroyed; a credit or unwind without a matching debit would be money created.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of all the banks' book balances plus the total amount riding the wire always equals the day's float exactly, so settlement never creates or destroys money.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every cutover the settlement enters eventually finishes and returns the batch to the open stage.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m7p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

\* Each blood unit carries a compare-and-swap cell holding its state and a
\* stamp that ticks on every successful swap.  Issuing is irreversible, and
\* the issue slip pins the exact stamp the unit had when it went out.
CONSTANTS Units, Techs, MaxStamp, MaxSlips

NoJob == "nojob"

VARIABLES cell, slips, job, saw, up
vars == <<cell, slips, job, saw, up>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ cell \in [Units -> [state: {"stock", "held", "issued"}, stamp: 0..MaxStamp]]
  /\ slips \in Seq([u: Units, stamp: 0..MaxStamp])
  /\ job \in [Techs -> Units \cup {NoJob}]
  /\ saw \in [Techs -> 0..MaxStamp]
  /\ up \in [Techs -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ cell = [u \in Units |-> [state |-> "stock", stamp |-> 0]]
  /\ slips = <<>>
  /\ job = [t \in Techs |-> NoJob]
  /\ saw = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ up = [t \in Techs |-> TRUE]

Abandoned(u) ==
  cell[u].state = "held" /\ ~(\E t \in Techs : up[t] /\ job[t] = u)

\* Swapping a unit from stock to held reserves it and ticks its stamp.
Reserve(t) ==
  /\ up[t] /\ job[t] = NoJob
  /\ \E u \in Units :
       /\ cell[u].state = "stock" /\ cell[u].stamp < MaxStamp
       /\ cell' = [cell EXCEPT ![u] = [state |-> "held", stamp |-> @.stamp + 1]]
       /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![t] = u]
       /\ saw' = [saw EXCEPT ![t] = cell[u].stamp + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slips, up>>

\* The irreversible step, guarded by the stamp the technician swapped in.
Issue(t) ==
  /\ up[t] /\ job[t] # NoJob
  /\ cell[job[t]].state = "held"
  /\ cell[job[t]].stamp = saw[t]
  /\ cell[job[t]].stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ Len(slips) < MaxSlips
  /\ cell' = [cell EXCEPT ![job[t]] = [state |-> "issued", stamp |-> @.stamp + 1]]
  /\ slips' = Append(slips, [u |-> job[t], stamp |-> cell[job[t]].stamp + 1])
  /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![t] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<saw, up>>

\* A technician can go down without telling anyone, holding a unit.
Collapse(t) ==
  /\ up[t]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cell, slips, job, saw>>

Return(t) ==
  /\ ~up[t]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
  /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![t] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cell, slips, saw>>

\* The sweeper swaps an orphaned reservation back to stock, ticking the
\* stamp so any technician still holding the old stamp is locked out.
Sweep ==
  /\ \E u \in Units :
       /\ Abandoned(u) /\ cell[u].stamp < MaxStamp
       /\ cell' = [cell EXCEPT ![u] = [state |-> "stock", stamp |-> @.stamp + 1]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slips, job, saw, up>>

Next == Sweep \/ \E t \in Techs : Reserve(t) \/ Issue(t) \/ Collapse(t) \/ Return(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every issue slip still matches its unit's cell exactly -- same issued
\* state, same stamp.  A second issue of that unit would tick the stamp and
\* leave the earlier slip pointing at a stamp the cell no longer carries.
SlipStillMatches ==
  \A i \in 1..Len(slips) :
    /\ cell[slips[i].u].state = "issued"
    /\ cell[slips[i].u].stamp = slips[i].stamp
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Units = {ua, ub}
  Techs = {tech1, tech2}
  MaxStamp = 3
  MaxSlips = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SlipStillMatches
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards every labelled unit with its own compare-and-swap cell. The cell holds the unit's state -- in stock, held, or issued -- together with a stamp that ticks up on every successful swap. Issuing a unit is irreversible: it goes to a patient and never comes back. When a unit is issued the tracker writes an issue slip pinning the unit and the exact stamp the cell carried at that moment.

The state is the cell for each unit, the sequence of issue slips, the unit each technician is working on (or none), the stamp each technician saw when it reserved that unit, and whether each technician is up.

There are five actions. Reserve fires for an up technician with no current unit: some unit reading in stock has its cell swapped to held with the stamp ticked, the technician records the unit as its job and remembers the new stamp. Issue is the irreversible step and fires only when the technician is up, its unit's cell still reads held, and the cell's stamp is still exactly the stamp the technician remembered: the cell is swapped to issued with the stamp ticked, an issue slip is appended pinning the unit and that new stamp, and the technician's job clears. Collapse models a technician going down without telling anyone, still nominally holding its unit. Return brings a downed technician back up with its job cleared, so the unit it was holding is now orphaned. Sweep is the recovery path: a held unit that no live technician is working on is swapped back to stock with its stamp ticked, and that tick is precisely what locks out any technician still carrying the old stamp.

The stamp is the whole defence. A technician that came back from a crash and tried to finish an old reservation would be swapping against a stamp the cell has already moved past.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every issue slip still matches its unit's cell exactly -- the cell reads issued and carries the very stamp the slip pinned -- so no unit is ever issued a second time, because a second issue would tick the stamp and strand the earlier slip.

---- MODULE W4Od1m7p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* The runway strip is a compare-and-swap cell naming the controller of
\* record plus a fence token.  Every clearance is stamped with the token the
\* issuing controller was carrying, which may lag if that desk is slow.
CONSTANTS Controllers, Flights, MaxFence, MaxIdle

Vacant == "vacant"

VARIABLES strip, token, onStrip, cleared, idling
vars == <<strip, token, onStrip, cleared, idling>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ strip \in [owner: Controllers \cup {Vacant}, fence: 0..MaxFence]
  /\ token \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxFence]
  /\ onStrip \subseteq Flights
  /\ cleared \in [Flights -> 0..MaxFence]
  /\ idling \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxIdle]

Init ==
  /\ strip = [owner |-> Vacant, fence |-> 0]
  /\ token = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ onStrip = {}
  /\ cleared = [f \in Flights |-> 0]
  /\ idling = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]

\* Handover swaps the strip to a new controller and burns a fence token.
\* It is only allowed with the runway physically empty.
Handover(c) ==
  /\ onStrip = {}
  /\ strip.fence < MaxFence
  /\ strip' = [owner |-> c, fence |-> strip.fence + 1]
  /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![c] = strip.fence + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onStrip, cleared, idling>>

\* A slow desk eventually reads the new fence off the strip.
Refresh(c) ==
  /\ token[c] < strip.fence
  /\ token' = [token EXCEPT ![c] = strip.fence]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, onStrip, cleared, idling>>

\* A clearance is stamped with the issuing desk's own token, not the strip's.
Clear(c) ==
  /\ strip.owner = c
  /\ token[c] = strip.fence
  /\ \E f \in Flights :
       /\ f \notin onStrip
       /\ onStrip' = onStrip \cup {f}
       /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![f] = token[c]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, token, idling>>

Rollout ==
  /\ \E f \in onStrip : onStrip' = onStrip \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, token, cleared, idling>>

\* A slow desk simply lets time pass without acting on anything.
Dawdle(c) ==
  /\ idling[c] < MaxIdle
  /\ idling' = [idling EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<strip, token, onStrip, cleared>>

Catchup == \E c \in Controllers : Refresh(c)

Next == \E c \in Controllers :
  Handover(c) \/ Refresh(c) \/ Clear(c) \/ Rollout \/ Dawdle(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Catchup)

\* Every aircraft standing on the runway was cleared under the fence token
\* the strip carries right now, so no lagging desk's clearance is ever left
\* holding the runway across a handover.
NoStaleClearance == \A f \in onStrip : cleared[f] = strip.fence

LaggingDesksCatchUp ==
  \A c \in Controllers : (token[c] < strip.fence) ~> (token[c] = strip.fence)
====

CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {deskA, deskB}
  Flights = {kl9, sk4}
  MaxFence = 2
  MaxIdle = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleClearance

PROPERTY LaggingDesksCatchUp
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator records who is in charge of a runway in a single compare-and-swap strip holding the controller of record together with a fence token. Every time the runway changes hands the strip is swapped to the incoming controller and the fence token is burned and replaced with a higher one. Each controller desk also carries its own copy of the token, and some desks are slow: they are not broken and they will read the strip eventually, but they can lag behind the live fence for a while.

The state is the strip, each desk's copy of the token, the set of flights standing on the runway, the token each of those flights was cleared under, and a per-desk idling counter.

There are five actions. Handover swaps the strip to some controller and burns the fence token, advancing it by one; it is permitted only while the runway is physically empty and the fence has not reached its ceiling, and the incoming desk's own token copy is set to the new fence. Refresh is a lagging desk reading the current fence off the strip into its own copy. Clear puts a flight onto the runway: it fires only for the desk the strip names and only while that desk's own token copy equals the live fence, and it stamps the flight with the token the issuing desk was carrying -- not with the strip's value. Rollout takes some flight off the runway. Dawdle is a slow desk letting time pass, advancing its idling counter up to a ceiling and touching nothing else.

The stamping rule in Clear is deliberate. A desk operating on a lagging token would stamp its clearance with the old fence, and a handover performed while such a flight was still on the runway would leave an aircraft on the strip authorised by a controller who is no longer in charge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every flight standing on the runway carries exactly the fence token the strip holds right now, so no clearance issued by a lagging or superseded desk is ever left holding the runway.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every controller desk whose token copy has fallen behind the live fence eventually reads the live fence.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Releasing a bay's twistlocks is a two-phase commit across the deck crews,
\* and it is irreversible -- the gear is cut, not unbolted.  The number of
\* bays a single round may cover is re-rated by the deck officer at runtime.
CONSTANTS Bays, Crews, MaxSweep, MaxRounds

VARIABLES stage, sweep, ballot, freed, allowed, rounds
vars == <<stage, sweep, ballot, freed, allowed, rounds>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ stage \in {"idle", "polling"}
  /\ sweep \subseteq Bays
  /\ ballot \in [Crews -> {"open", "aye", "nay"}]
  /\ freed \subseteq Bays
  /\ allowed \in 1..MaxSweep
  /\ rounds \in 0..MaxRounds

Init ==
  /\ stage = "idle"
  /\ sweep = {}
  /\ ballot = [c \in Crews |-> "open"]
  /\ freed = {}
  /\ allowed = MaxSweep
  /\ rounds = 0

\* A round may only be opened over bays whose gear is still intact.
Propose ==
  /\ stage = "idle"
  /\ rounds < MaxRounds
  /\ \E S \in SUBSET Bays :
       /\ S # {}
       /\ S \cap freed = {}
       /\ Cardinality(S) =< allowed
       /\ sweep' = S
  /\ stage' = "polling"
  /\ ballot' = [c \in Crews |-> "open"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<freed, allowed, rounds>>

Vote(c) ==
  /\ stage = "polling"
  /\ ballot[c] = "open"
  /\ \E v \in {"aye", "nay"} : ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, sweep, freed, allowed, rounds>>

\* Unanimity cuts the gear on every bay in the round, once and for good.
Commit ==
  /\ stage = "polling"
  /\ \A c \in Crews : ballot[c] = "aye"
  /\ freed' = freed \cup sweep
  /\ sweep' = {}
  /\ stage' = "idle"
  /\ rounds' = rounds + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, allowed>>

Rollback ==
  /\ stage = "polling"
  /\ \E c \in Crews : ballot[c] = "nay"
  /\ sweep' = {}
  /\ stage' = "idle"
  /\ rounds' = rounds + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, freed, allowed>>

\* The deck officer re-rates how wide a single round may be, at any time.
Rerate ==
  /\ \E n \in 1..MaxSweep : n # allowed /\ allowed' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, sweep, ballot, freed, rounds>>

Next == Propose \/ Commit \/ Rollback \/ Rerate \/ \E c \in Crews : Vote(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No live round ever overlaps a bay whose twistlocks have already been cut,
\* so the irreversible release happens at most once per bay.
CutOncePerBay == (stage = "polling") => (sweep \cap freed = {})
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Bays = {bay1, bay2, bay3}
  Crews = {lash, gantry}
  MaxSweep = 2
  MaxRounds = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CutOncePerBay
nl:
A container-ship crane yard releases the twistlocks that hold containers down in a bay. Cutting a bay's gear is irreversible: the locks are cut away rather than unbolted, so a bay can be released exactly once and never re-secured within the operation. Because several deck crews have to agree before anything is cut, the release runs as a two-phase commit: a round is proposed over a set of bays, every crew votes, and only unanimous agreement cuts the gear. The deck officer also re-rates at runtime how many bays a single round is allowed to cover.

The state is the stage (idle or polling), the set of bays the live round covers, each crew's ballot (open, aye, or nay), the set of bays whose gear has already been cut, the current per-round bay allowance, and a round counter.

There are five actions. Propose fires while idle and below the round ceiling: it picks a non-empty set of bays that is disjoint from the already-cut set and no larger than the current allowance, makes that the round's sweep, moves to polling, and resets every crew's ballot to open. Vote lets a crew with an open ballot record aye or nay. Commit fires while polling once every crew has voted aye: every bay in the sweep has its gear cut and joins the already-cut set, the sweep empties, the round counter advances, and the yard returns to idle. Rollback fires while polling once any crew has voted nay: the sweep is abandoned with nothing cut, the round counter advances, and the yard returns to idle. Rerate sets the per-round bay allowance to any different value in range, whether or not a round is live.

The disjointness check inside Propose is the whole safeguard. A round that reached across a bay whose gear was already cut would commit a second cut on hardware that is no longer there.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a round is being polled, the set of bays it covers is disjoint from the set of bays whose twistlocks have already been cut, so the irreversible release is committed at most once for any bay.

---- MODULE W4Od4m0p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* App bookings and kiosk bookings share one pool of conveyor bays.  A car
\* reads a free bay off the bay map, then commits only if the map's revision
\* has not moved -- the revision check is the whole defence.
CONSTANTS AppCars, KioskCars, Bays, MaxRev, MaxRetry

Cars == AppCars \cup KioskCars
NoBay == "nobay"
Anchor == CHOOSE b \in Bays : TRUE

VARIABLES booking, mapRev, draft, retry, standing
vars == <<booking, mapRev, draft, retry, standing>>

Taken == {booking[c] : c \in Cars} \ {NoBay}
Holders == {c \in Cars : booking[c] # NoBay}

TypeOK ==
  /\ booking \in [Cars -> Bays \cup {NoBay}]
  /\ mapRev \in 0..MaxRev
  /\ draft \in [Cars -> [bay: Bays, snap: 0..MaxRev]]
  /\ retry \in [Cars -> 0..MaxRetry]
  /\ standing \in [Cars -> {"waiting", "trying", "parked", "gone"}]

Init ==
  /\ booking = [c \in Cars |-> NoBay]
  /\ mapRev = 0
  /\ draft = [c \in Cars |-> [bay |-> Anchor, snap |-> 0]]
  /\ retry = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ standing = [c \in Cars |-> "waiting"]

Bookable(c) == standing[c] = "trying" /\ draft[c].snap = mapRev /\ mapRev < MaxRev

\* Reading the map: pick a bay that looks free right now, note the revision.
Read(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "waiting"
  /\ \E b \in Bays :
       /\ b \notin Taken
       /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![c] = [bay |-> b, snap |-> mapRev]]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "trying"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booking, mapRev, retry>>

\* Commit trusts the revision, not a fresh look at the map.
Park(c) ==
  /\ Bookable(c)
  /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![c] = draft[c].bay]
  /\ mapRev' = mapRev + 1
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "parked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, retry>>

Reread(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "trying" /\ ~Bookable(c) /\ retry[c] < MaxRetry
  /\ retry' = [retry EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booking, mapRev, draft>>

DriveOff(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "trying" /\ ~Bookable(c) /\ retry[c] = MaxRetry
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "gone"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booking, mapRev, draft, retry>>

Exit(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "parked"
  /\ mapRev < MaxRev
  /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![c] = NoBay]
  /\ mapRev' = mapRev + 1
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "gone"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<draft, retry>>

\* Nothing free to read: the car leaves the site rather than idling.
Balk(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "waiting"
  /\ \A b \in Bays : b \in Taken
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "gone"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booking, mapRev, draft, retry>>

Closed == (\A c \in Cars : standing[c] \in {"parked", "gone"}) /\ UNCHANGED vars

Decide == \E c \in Cars : Park(c) \/ Reread(c) \/ DriveOff(c)
Next == Decide \/ Closed \/ \E c \in Cars : Read(c) \/ Exit(c) \/ Balk(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Decide)

\* The booking map is injective: as many distinct bays are booked as there
\* are cars holding a booking, so no conveyor bay is ever handed to two cars.
NoDoubleBooking == Cardinality(Taken) = Cardinality(Holders)

TryingCarsDecide == \A c \in Cars : (standing[c] = "trying") ~> (standing[c] # "trying")
====
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a fixed set of conveyor bays. Two independent booking channels -- the phone app and the drive-up kiosk -- send cars at the same bays; neither channel has bays of its own, they share one pool. There is no lock on the bay map. Instead the map carries a revision number, and a car books optimistically: it reads a bay that looks free together with the map's revision, then commits, and the commit succeeds only if the revision has not moved in the meantime.

The state is the bay each car has booked (or none), the map revision, each car's draft (the bay it read and the revision it read), a per-car retry allowance, and each car's standing: waiting, trying, parked, or gone.

There are seven actions. Read fires for a waiting car: it picks some bay that is not currently booked by anybody, writes that bay and the live revision into its draft, and becomes trying. A trying car is bookable when the revision in its draft still equals the live revision and the map has not reached its final revision. Park fires on a bookable car: its booking is set to the bay in its draft, the map revision advances by one, and the car becomes parked -- note that Park trusts the revision rather than taking a fresh look at the map, which is exactly what makes the revision check load-bearing. Reread fires on a trying car that is not bookable and still has retry allowance: it spends one retry and drops back to waiting. DriveOff fires on a trying car that is not bookable with its allowance spent, and the car leaves. Exit fires for a parked car while the map has room: its booking is released, the revision advances, and the car leaves. Balk fires for a waiting car when every bay is already booked, and the car leaves rather than idling. Closed applies once every car is either parked or gone and leaves the line exactly as it stands.

A conveyor bay holds one car. Two cars sent to the same bay by the two channels would collide on the track.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of distinct bays currently booked always equals the number of cars currently holding a booking, so the booking map is injective and no conveyor bay is ever allocated to two cars at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car that starts trying to commit a booking eventually stops trying, whether by parking, by re-reading the map, or by driving off.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m2p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A fleet-wide price change runs as a two-phase commit over a radio pool
\* with no ordering at all.  Votes and go-orders from an earlier round can
\* still be floating around when the next round opens.
CONSTANTS Machines, MaxRound, PoolCap

VARIABLES round, phase, quorum, installed, pool
vars == <<round, phase, quorum, installed, pool>>

Notes == [kind: {"vote", "go"}, who: Machines, rnd: 0..MaxRound]

Stale(m) ==
  \/ m.rnd # round
  \/ (m.kind = "vote" /\ phase # "polling")
  \/ (m.kind = "go" /\ phase # "closing")

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
  /\ phase \in {"polling", "closing"}
  /\ quorum \subseteq Machines
  /\ installed \subseteq Machines
  /\ pool \subseteq Notes

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ phase = "polling"
  /\ quorum = {}
  /\ installed = {}
  /\ pool = {}

\* Opening a round clears the tallies but leaves the radio pool untouched.
Open ==
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ phase' = "polling"
  /\ quorum' = {}
  /\ installed' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED pool

\* Machines transmit whenever they like, stamping the round they know of.
Transmit ==
  /\ Cardinality(pool) < PoolCap
  /\ \E w \in Machines : \E r \in 0..round :
       pool' = pool \cup {[kind |-> "vote", who |-> w, rnd |-> r]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, quorum, installed>>

Tally ==
  /\ \E m \in pool :
       /\ m.kind = "vote" /\ phase = "polling" /\ m.rnd = round
       /\ quorum' = quorum \cup {m.who}
       /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, installed>>

\* Closing the poll sends a go-order to exactly the machines in the quorum.
Close ==
  /\ phase = "polling"
  /\ quorum # {}
  /\ Cardinality(pool) + Cardinality(quorum) =< PoolCap
  /\ phase' = "closing"
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {[kind |-> "go", who |-> w, rnd |-> round] : w \in quorum}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, quorum, installed>>

Install ==
  /\ \E m \in pool :
       /\ m.kind = "go" /\ phase = "closing" /\ m.rnd = round
       /\ installed' = installed \cup {m.who}
       /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, quorum>>

Discard ==
  /\ \E m \in pool : Stale(m) /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, phase, quorum, installed>>

Next == Open \/ Transmit \/ Tally \/ Close \/ Install \/ Discard

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Only machines the coordinator tallied into the current round's quorum
\* ever install the new price: a go-order left over from an older round
\* never authorises a machine in this one.
NoUnauthorisedInstall == installed \subseteq quorum
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Machines = {vm1, vm2}
  MaxRound = 2
  PoolCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoUnauthorisedInstall
nl:
A vending machine network rolls out a fleet-wide price change as a two-phase commit. A coordinator opens a numbered round, machines vote, the coordinator closes the poll and sends a go-order to exactly the machines it tallied, and those machines install the new price. Everything travels over a shared radio pool of bounded size that provides no ordering whatsoever: a vote or a go-order transmitted during one round can still be floating in the pool when the next round has already opened.

The state is the round number, the phase (polling or closing), the quorum the coordinator has tallied for the current round, the set of machines that have installed the new price in the current round, and the radio pool.

A pooled message counts as stale when its round stamp differs from the live round, or it is a vote arriving outside the polling phase, or it is a go-order arriving outside the closing phase.

There are six actions. Open advances the round number, returns the phase to polling, and clears both the quorum and the installed set -- but deliberately leaves the radio pool untouched, so older traffic survives into the new round. Transmit fires whenever the pool has room: some machine puts a vote into the pool stamped with any round number up to the live one, which is how a machine running behind gets modelled. Tally takes a vote out of the pool that is stamped with the live round while the phase is polling and adds its sender to the quorum. Close fires while polling with a non-empty quorum and enough pool room: the phase becomes closing and one go-order stamped with the live round is placed in the pool for each machine in the quorum, and for nobody else. Install takes a go-order out of the pool that is stamped with the live round while the phase is closing and records its addressee as having installed the new price. Discard removes any stale message from the pool.

The round stamp on the go-order is the only thing separating an authorised install from an unauthorised one. A machine that acted on a go-order left over from a previous round would be changing its prices on the strength of an authorisation the coordinator has already retracted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every machine that has installed the new price is a machine the coordinator tallied into the current round's quorum, so no machine ever acts on a stale or unauthorised go-order.
